尒硃榮子文暢文略從子兆從弟彥伯彥伯子敞彥伯弟仲遠世隆榮從父弟度律榮從祖兄子天光
Erzhu Rong; his sons Wenchang and Wenlue; his nephew Zhao; his cousins Yanbo, Yanbo's son Chang, Yanbo's brother Zhongyuan, and Shilong; Rong's paternal cousin Dulu; and Rong's grand-uncle's grandson Tianguang.
2
尒硃榮
Erzhu Rong
3
尒硃榮，字天寶，北秀容人也。 世為部落酋帥，其先居尒硃川，因為氏焉。 高祖羽健，魏登國初為領人酋長，率契胡武士從平晉陽，定中山，拜散騎常侍。 以居秀容川，詔割方三百里封之，長為世業。 道武初，以南秀容川原沃衍，欲令居之。 羽健曰：「家世奉國，給侍左右，北秀容既在髂內，差近京師，豈以沃鹆脊，更遷遠地？ 」帝許之。 所居處曾有狗舐地，因而穿之得甘泉，因名狗舐泉。 曾祖鬱德、祖代勤，繼為酋長。 代勤，太武敬哀皇后舅也。 既以外親，兼數征伐有功，給復百年，除立義將軍。 曾圍山而獵，部人射虎，誤中其髀。 代勤仍令拔箭，竟不推問，曰：「此既過誤，何忍加罪。 」部內咸感其意。 位肆州刺史，封梁郡公，以老致仕，歲賜帛百疋以為常。 卒，諡曰莊。 孝莊初，追贈太師、司徒公、錄尚書事。 父新興，太和中繼為酋長。 曾行馬群，見一白蛇，頭有兩角，咒之，求畜牧蕃息。 自是牛羊駝馬，日覺滋盛，色別為群，穀量之。 朝廷每有征討，輒獻私馬，兼備資糧，助裨軍用。 孝文嘉之。 及遷洛，特聽冬朝京師，夏歸部落。 每入朝，諸公王朝貴，競以珍玩遺之，新興亦報以名馬。 位散騎常侍、平北將軍、秀容第一領人酋長。 新興每春秋二時，恆與妻子閱畜牧于川澤，射獵自娛。 明帝時，以年老，啟求傳爵于榮。 卒，諡曰簡。 孝莊初，贈太師、相國、西河郡王。
Erzhu Rong, whose style name was Tianbao, came from Northern Xiurong. His family had served for generations as tribal chieftains. Their forebears had settled on the Erzhu River and adopted it as their clan name. His great-grandfather Yu Jian, in the early years of Emperor Daowu's Dengguo reign, was Leader-Chief of the Lingren. He led Qihu warriors in the campaigns that pacified Jinyang and secured Zhongshan, and was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry. Because the family lived on the Xiurong River, the throne granted them a domain of three hundred square li, which became their hereditary holding for generations. Early in Emperor Daowu's reign, seeing that the plains around Southern Xiurong River were rich and open, he wanted the clan to relocate there. Yu Jian replied: "Our house has served the dynasty for generations, attending at the sovereign's side. Northern Xiurong already lies within the capital region and is comparatively near the court. How could we be uprooted to distant country simply for richer land? " The emperor agreed. At their settlement a dog once licked the ground; when they dug there they found a sweet spring, and the place came to be called Dog-Lick Spring. His great-great-grandfather Yude and his grandfather Dai Qin each in turn held the chieftainship. Dai Qin was a maternal uncle of Emperor Taiwu's Empress Jing'ai. As a kinsman by marriage and a man who had repeatedly distinguished himself in battle, he was granted a century of corvée exemption and appointed General Who Establishes Righteousness. Once, while hunting in the hills, a tribesman fired at a tiger and accidentally hit Dai Qin in the thigh. Dai Qin had the arrow drawn out and never pressed an inquiry. "This was plainly an accident," he said. "How could I bear to punish the man? " Everyone in the tribe was moved by his forbearance. He served as Governor of Sizhou and was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang Commandery. When he retired on account of age, the court made it his regular stipend to receive a hundred bolts of silk each year. At his death he was given the posthumous name Zhuang. Early in Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing. His father Xinxing succeeded to the chieftainship during the Taihe era. Once, while driving his horses, he saw a white serpent with two horns on its head. He prayed over it, asking that his herds might flourish. From that time his cattle, sheep, camels, and horses grew ever more numerous. Sorted by color into separate herds, they were counted by the bushel. Whenever the court went to war, he presented horses from his own herds and supplied provisions to bolster the army. Emperor Xiaowen praised him for this. After the capital was moved to Luoyang, he received special permission to attend court in the capital each winter and return to his tribe each summer. Whenever he came to court, princes, dukes, and great nobles competed to send him rare treasures, and Xinxing repaid them with fine horses. He held the posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and First Leader-Chief of Xiurong. Each spring and autumn Xinxing would take his wife and children to inspect the herds in the rivers and marshes and pass the time hunting. During Emperor Ming's reign, feeling his age, he petitioned to pass his title to Rong. At his death he was given the posthumous name Jian. Early in Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Chancellor of State, and King of Xihe Commandery.
4
榮潔白，美容貌，幼而神機明決。 及長，好射獵，每設圍誓眾，便為軍陣之法，號令嚴肅，眾莫敢犯。 秀容界有池三所，在高山上，清深不測，相傳曰祁連池，魏言天池也。 父新興曾與榮游池上，忽聞簫鼓音，謂榮曰：「古老相傳，聞此聲，皆至公輔。 吾年老暮，當為汝耳。 」榮襲爵，後除直寢、遊擊將軍。 正光中，四方兵起，遂散畜牧，招合義勇。 以討賊功，進封博陵郡公，其梁郡前爵聽賜第二子。 時榮率眾至肆州，刺史尉慶賓閉城不納。 榮怒，攻拔之，乃署其從叔羽生為刺史，執慶賓還秀容。 自是兵威漸盛，朝廷亦不能罪責。 及葛榮吞杜洛周，榮恐其南逼鄴城，表求東援相州，帝不許。 榮以山東賊盛，慮其西逸，乃遣兵固守滏口以防之。 於是北捍馬邑，東塞井陘。 尋屬明帝崩，事出倉卒，榮乃與元天穆等密議，入匡朝廷。 抗表云：「今海內草草，異口一言，皆云大行皇帝鴆毒致禍，舉潘嬪之女以誑百姓，奉未言之兒而臨四海。 求以徐紇、鄭儼之徒，付之司敗。 更召宗親，推其明德。 」於是將赴京師。 靈太后甚懼，詔以李神軌為大都督，將于太行杜防。 榮抗表之始，遣從子天光、親信奚毅及倉頭王相入洛，與從弟世隆密議廢立。 天光乃見莊帝，具論榮心，帝許之。 天光等還北，榮發晉陽，猶疑所立，乃以銅鑄孝文及咸陽王禧等五王子孫像，成者當奉為主。 唯莊帝獨就。 師次河內，重遣王相密迎莊帝與帝兄彭城王邵、弟始平王子正。 武泰元年四月，莊帝自高渚度，至榮軍，將士咸稱萬歲。
Rong was fair-skinned and handsome, and even as a boy showed a sharp and resolute mind. As a man he loved hunting. Whenever he organized a hunt and gathered his followers, he drilled them in battle formation. His orders were strict, and no one dared defy them. Within Xiurong territory stood three pools on high mountains, clear and fathomlessly deep. Tradition called them the Qilian Pools; in the Wei tongue they were known as the Heavenly Pools. His father Xinxing once walked with Rong beside one of the pools when they suddenly heard flute and drum music. He told Rong: "The old tradition says that whoever hears this sound will rise to the highest offices of state. I am old now and near my end; the omen must be meant for you. " Rong succeeded to the title and was later appointed Attendant of the Direct Quarters and General of Roaming Attack. During the Zhengguang era, when rebellion flared on every side, he broke up his herds and rallied volunteers to arms. For his service in suppressing rebels he was promoted to Duke of Boling Commandery, while his former title of Liang Commandery was granted to his second son. At that time Rong led his troops to Sizhou, but Governor Wei Qingbin closed the city gates and refused them entry. Enraged, Rong stormed and captured the city. He installed his uncle Yusheng as governor, took Qingbin prisoner, and returned to Xiurong. From that point his military power steadily grew, and the court was in no position to hold him accountable. When Ge Rong absorbed Du Luozhou's forces, Rong feared a southern thrust against Ye City and petitioned to march east and relieve Xiang Province, but the emperor refused. Seeing the rebels strong in the east, Rong feared they might break westward and sent troops to hold Fukou against them. He therefore defended Mayi in the north and blocked Jingxing Pass in the east. Soon afterward Emperor Ming died suddenly. Rong then secretly consulted with Yuan Tianmu and others about marching on the capital to restore order at court. He submitted a defiant memorial saying: "The realm is in uproar, and everywhere one hears the same story: that the late emperor was poisoned, that Pan Consort's daughter has been put forward to deceive the people, and that an infant who cannot yet speak has been set to rule the empire. I ask that Xu He, Zheng Yan, and their accomplices be handed over to the Office of Punishment. Summon the imperial clansmen again and set up a ruler of proven virtue. " He then prepared to march on the capital. Empress Dowager Ling was terrified and ordered Li Shengui appointed Grand Commander to lead troops and block him at the Taihang passes. As soon as Rong submitted his defiant memorial, he sent his nephew Tianguang, his trusted follower Xi Yi, and the steward Wang Xiang into Luoyang to confer secretly with his cousin Shilong on deposing the old ruler and enthroning a new one. Tianguang then met with the future Emperor Xiaozhuang and laid out Rong's plan in full; the prince agreed. When Tianguang and the others returned north, Rong marched out from Jinyang. Still uncertain whom to enthrone, he cast bronze images of Emperor Xiaowen and of the descendants of the five princes, including Prince Xianyang of Xianyang. Whoever among them cast successfully would be made sovereign. Only the image of the future Emperor Xiaozhuang came out whole. When the army halted at Henei, he again sent Wang Xiang secretly to bring out the future emperor, his elder brother Prince Shao of Pengcheng, and his younger brother Prince Zizheng of Shiping. In the fourth month of the first year of Wutai, the future emperor crossed from Gaozhu and reached Rong's camp. Officers and soldiers alike shouted "Long live the emperor!"
5
及莊帝即位，詔以榮為使持節、都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、開府、尚書令、領軍將軍、領左右、太原王。 及度河，太后乃下發入道，內外百官皆向河橋迎駕。 榮惑武衛將軍費穆之言，謂天下乘機可取，乃譎朝士共為盟誓，將向河陰西北三里。 至南北長堤，悉命下馬西度，即遣胡騎四面圍之。 妄言丞相高陽王欲反，殺百官王公卿士二千餘人，皆斂手就戮。 又命二三十人拔刀走行宮。 莊帝及彭城王、霸城王俱出帳。 榮先遣并州人郭羅察共西部高車叱列殺鬼在帝左右，相與為應。 及見事起，假言防衛，抱帝入帳，餘人即害彭城、霸城二王。 乃令四五十人遷帝於河橋，沉靈太后及少主於河。 時又有朝士百餘人後至，仍於堤東被圍。 遂臨以白刃，唱云：「能為禪文者出，當原其命。 」時有隴西李神俊、頓丘李諧、太原溫子升並當世辭人，皆在圍中，恥是從命，俯伏不應。 有御史趙元則者，恐不免死，出作禪文。 榮令人誡軍士，言元氏既滅，尒硃氏興。 其眾咸稱萬歲。 榮遂鑄金為己像，數四不成。 時榮所信幽州人劉靈助善卜占，言今時人事未可。 榮乃曰：「若我作不吉，當迎天穆立之。 」靈助曰：「天穆亦不吉，唯長樂王有王兆耳。 」榮亦精神恍惚，不自支持，遂便愧悔。 至四更中，乃迎莊帝，望馬首叩頭請死。 其士馬三千餘騎，既濫殺朝士，乃不敢入京，即欲向北為移都之計。 持疑經日，始奉駕向洛陽宮。 及上北芒，視城闕，復懷畏懼，不肯更前。 武衛將軍汎禮苦執不聽，復前入城，不朝戍。 北來之人，皆乘馬入殿。 諸貴死散，無復次序。 莊帝左右，唯有故舊數人。 榮猶執移都之議，上亦無以拒焉。 又在明光殿重謝河橋之事，誓言無復二心。 莊帝自起止之，因復為榮誓，言無疑心。 榮喜，因求酒一遍。 及醉熟，帝欲誅之，左右苦諫乃止。 即以床輦向中常侍省。 榮夜半方寤，遂達旦不眠。 自此不復禁中宿矣。
When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, an edict appointed Rong Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside the Court, Grand General, Opener of an Office, Director of the Masters of Writing, General of the Guards, Director of the Left and Right, and King of Taiyuan. After they crossed the river, the empress dowager had her head shaved and entered religious life. Officials throughout the court went to Heqiao to welcome the imperial carriage. Rong was swayed by General of Martial Guards Fei Mu, who told him the realm could be seized at this moment. He deceived the court officials into swearing a joint oath of allegiance and led them toward a place three li northwest of Heyin. When they reached the north-south embankment, he ordered them all to dismount and cross to the west, then sent his barbarian cavalry to surround them on every side. Falsely claiming that Chancellor Prince Gao of Gaoyang intended rebellion, he slaughtered more than two thousand officials, princes, dukes, and ministers, every one of them submitting without a struggle. He also ordered twenty or thirty men to draw their swords and rush the traveling palace. Emperor Xiaozhuang, the Prince of Pengcheng, and the Prince of Bacheng all came out of the tent together. Rong had already placed the Bingzhou man Guo Luocha and Chilieshagui of the western Gao-che at the emperor's side to act in concert with the assailants. When the attack began, they pretended to be protecting him, seized the emperor, and carried him into the tent, while the others immediately killed the Princes of Pengcheng and Bacheng. He then ordered forty or fifty men to move the emperor to Heqiao and drowned Empress Dowager Ling and the young sovereign in the river. More than a hundred court officials who arrived later were likewise surrounded east of the embankment. They were then confronted with naked blades, and a voice cried out: "Whoever can compose an abdication document may come forward, and his life will be spared. " Longxi's Li Shenjun, Dunqiu's Li Xie, and Taiyuan's Wen Zisheng—all celebrated writers of the age—were among those surrounded. Too ashamed to obey, they prostrated themselves and said nothing. An investigating censor named Zhao Yuanze, fearing he could not escape death, came forward and composed the abdication document. Rong had a man instruct the soldiers: "The Yuan clan is destroyed; the Erzhu clan rises. " The troops all shouted "Long live!" Rong then tried to cast a golden image of himself, but after several attempts it would not come out right. At the time Liu Lingzhu of Youzhou, a diviner whom Rong trusted, said the moment was not favorable for such an undertaking. Rong then said: "If it is inauspicious for me to take the throne, then Tianmu should be brought in and enthroned. " Lingzhu said: "Tianmu is also inauspicious. Only the Prince of Changle shows the signs of kingship. " Rong too was dazed and could not steady himself, and was overcome with shame and regret. By the fourth watch he welcomed Emperor Xiaozhuang back, bowed his head to the horse's neck, and begged to be put to death. His three thousand-odd horsemen, having wantonly slaughtered court officials, dared not enter the capital and at once planned to move north and relocate the court. After hesitating for several days, he finally escorted the imperial carriage toward the Luoyang palace. When they ascended Northern Mang and looked upon the city towers, he was seized by fear again and would go no farther. General of Martial Guards Fan Li pressed him earnestly but could not prevail. Rong went forward into the city but did not attend court the next morning. Those who had come from the north all rode their horses into the hall. The great nobles were dead or scattered, and court order had collapsed. At Emperor Xiaozhuang's side there remained only a few old associates. Rong still clung to the plan to move the capital, and the emperor had no way to refuse. In Mingguang Hall he apologized again for the massacre at Heqiao and swore he would never again harbor divided loyalties. Emperor Xiaozhuang himself rose to stop him and in turn swore an oath to Rong, saying he harbored no suspicion. Rong was pleased and asked for wine to be passed around. When he was thoroughly drunk, the emperor wished to execute him, but those at his side earnestly remonstrated and stopped him. He was then carried on a couch-litter to the Directorate of Palace Attendants. Rong did not wake until midnight and then lay awake until dawn. From then on he never again slept within the palace precincts.
6
榮女先為明帝嬪，欲上立為後，帝疑未決。 給事黃門侍郎祖瑩曰：「昔文公在秦，懷嬴入侍。 事有反經合義，陛下獨何疑焉？ 」上遂從之。 榮意甚悅。 于時，人間猶或云榮欲遷都晉陽，或云欲肆兵大掠，迭相驚恐，人情駭震。 京邑士子，十不一存，率皆逃竄，無敢出者，直衛空虛，官守廢曠。 榮聞之，上書謝愆。 無上王請追尊帝號； 諸王、刺史，乞贈三司； 其位班三品，請贈令僕； 五品之官，各贈方伯； 六品已下及白身，贈以鎮郡。 諸死者無後，聽繼，即授封爵。 均其高下，節級別科，使恩洽存亡，有慰生死。 詔從所表。 又啟帝，遣使巡城勞問。 於是人情遂安，朝士逃亡者，亦稍來歸闕。 榮又奏請番直，朔望之日，引見三公、令、僕、尚書、九卿及司州牧、河南尹、洛陽河陰執事之官，參論國政，以為常式。
Rong's daughter had earlier been a consort of Emperor Ming. Rong wanted the emperor to make her empress, but the emperor hesitated and had not decided. Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zu Ying said: "In antiquity, when Duke Wen of Jin was in Qin, Huai Ying entered his service. There are times when what runs counter to convention still accords with righteousness. Why should Your Majesty alone hesitate? " The emperor then followed his advice. Rong was greatly pleased. At that time people still whispered that Rong meant to move the capital to Jinyang, or that he intended to unleash his troops in a great pillaging. Alarm followed alarm, and public sentiment was shaken with terror. Of the scholar-officials in the capital, scarcely one in ten remained. Most had fled and gone into hiding, and none dared show themselves. The palace guard posts stood empty, and government offices were left unattended. When Rong heard of this, he submitted a memorial apologizing for what he had done. For the Prince of Supreme, he asked that posthumous imperial honors be granted; for princes and provincial inspectors, he requested posthumous appointment to the Three Excellencies; for those whose rank stood at the third grade or above, he requested posthumous appointment as Ministers-in-Chief and Masters of Writing; for officials of the fifth grade, he requested that each be granted a posthumous title equivalent to a regional governor; for those of the sixth grade and below, and for commoners without office, he requested posthumous titles as commandery and district magistrates. For the dead who left no heirs, he allowed successors to be appointed and immediately granted them titles and fiefs. He balanced high and low, assigning honors by rank in graduated categories, so that imperial grace would reach both the living and the dead and bring consolation to the bereaved. An edict approved his petition. He also reported to the emperor and sent envoys to tour the city, offering reassurance and inquiry to the people. Thereupon public sentiment calmed, and court officials who had fled also gradually returned to the capital. Rong further petitioned to establish a rotating attendance duty. On the first and fifteenth of each month he would summon the Three Excellencies, Ministers-in-Chief, Masters of Writing, the Nine Ministers, the Governor of Sizhou, the Intendant of Henan, and the officials responsible at Luoyang and Heyin to discuss state affairs, making this a standing practice.
7
五月，榮還晉陽，乃令元天穆向京，為侍中、太尉公、錄尚書事、京畿大都督，兼領軍將軍，封上党王，樹置腹心在列職，舉止所為，皆由其意。 七月，詔加榮柱國大將軍。
In the fifth month Rong returned to Jinyang and sent Yuan Tianmu to the capital, appointing him Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Commander of the Capital Region, and concurrently General Who Leads the Army, with the title Prince of Shangdang. He placed trusted intimates in every office, and their conduct and actions all followed his will. In the seventh month an edict promoted Rong to Grand General Who Is the Pillar of the State.
8
時葛榮向京師，眾號百萬。 州刺史李神俊閉門自守。 榮率精騎七千，馬皆有副，倍道兼行，東出滏口。 而與葛榮眾寡非敵。 葛榮聞之，喜見於色，乃令其眾辦長繩，至便縛取。 自鄴以北，列陣數十里，箕張而進。 榮潛軍山谷為奇兵，分督將已上三人為一處，處有數百騎，令所在揚塵鼓噪，使賊不測多少。 又以人馬逼戰，刀不如棒。 密勒軍士，馬上各齎袖棒一枚，至戰時，慮廢騰逐，不聽斬級，使以棒，棒之而已。 乃分命壯勇，所當衝突。 號令嚴明，將士同奮。 身自陷陣，出於賊後，表裏合擊，大破之。 于陣禽葛榮，餘眾悉降。 榮恐其疑懼，乃普令各從所樂，親屬相隨，任所居止。 於是群情喜悅，登即四散，數十萬眾，一朝散盡。 待出百里之外，乃始分道押領，隨便安置，咸得其宜。 獲其渠帥，量才授用，新附者咸安。 時人服其處分機速。 乃檻車送葛榮赴闕。 詔加榮大丞相、都督河北畿外諸軍事。 初，榮將討葛榮，軍次襄垣，遂大獵，有雙兔起于馬前，榮彎弓誓之曰：「中則禽葛榮，不中則否。 」既而並應弦而殪，三軍咸悅。 及後，命立碑於其所，號雙兔碑。 又將戰，夜夢一人從葛榮索千牛刀，葛榮初不肯與，此人自稱己是道武皇帝，葛榮乃奉刀，此人手持授榮。 寤而喜。 自知必勝。 又詔以冀州之長樂、相州之南趙、定州之博陵、滄州之浮陽、平州之遼西、燕州之上穀、幽州之漁陽七郡，各萬戶，通前滿十萬。 為太原國邑，又加位太師。
At that time Ge Rong was marching on the capital, and his forces were said to number a million. The Xiangzhou inspector Li Shenjun closed his gates and held the city. Rong led seven thousand elite horsemen, each rider with a spare mount, and by forced marches day and night marched east through Fakou. Yet his force was far too small to match Ge Rong's army. When Ge Rong heard of this, his delight showed plainly on his face. He ordered his troops to prepare long ropes so that when Rong arrived they could bind and capture him alive. From Ye northward he drew up battle lines stretching for dozens of li and advanced with his wings spread wide. Rong hid troops in valleys and ravines as a surprise force, grouping commanders of colonel rank and above in threes at each position, each with several hundred horsemen, and ordering them to raise dust and make a clamor wherever they appeared so the enemy could not tell how many they faced. He also reasoned that in close combat between mounted men, blades were less effective than clubs. He secretly ordered every mounted soldier to carry a short club in his sleeve, and when battle came, fearing that the chase for severed heads would waste the momentum of pursuit, he forbade decapitation for tallying kills. They were simply to use the clubs and beat the enemy down. He then assigned the bravest and strongest men to the points where they would break through the enemy lines. His orders were strict and clear, and officers and soldiers fought as one. He himself plunged into the battle line and emerged behind the enemy, and his forces struck from front and rear together, inflicting a crushing defeat. In the battle he captured Ge Rong, and all the remaining troops surrendered. Fearing that the captives would grow suspicious and panic, Rong broadly ordered that each man might go where he pleased, with relatives free to follow, and settle wherever he chose. Thereupon the captives were delighted, and at once they scattered in all directions. Several hundred thousand men dispersed in a single morning. After they had gone a hundred li away, he then began to escort them in separate groups and settle them wherever appropriate, and all were placed suitably. The rebel leaders he captured he employed according to their abilities, and the newly submitted all felt secure. People of the time admired the speed and decisiveness with which he handled the matter. He then sent Ge Rong to the capital in a caged cart. An edict promoted Rong to Grand Chancellor and Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Hebei and beyond the capital region. Earlier, when Rong was about to campaign against Ge Rong, his army halted at Xiangyuan and then went on a great hunt. A pair of hares sprang up before his horse, and Rong bent his bow and swore: "If I hit them, I shall capture Ge Rong; if not, I shall not. " Both hares fell at the release of the bowstring, and the whole army rejoiced. Later he ordered a stele erected at that spot, called the Stele of the Two Hares. Again, on the eve of battle, he dreamed that a man demanded a thousand-cattle blade from Ge Rong. Ge Rong at first refused, but the man declared himself to be Emperor Daowu, whereupon Ge Rong surrendered the blade, and the man handed it to Rong. When he woke he was delighted. He knew that he was certain to win. An edict further granted him the seven commanderies of Changlo in Jizhou, Nanzhao in Xiangzhou, Boling in Dingzhou, Fuyang in Cangzhou, Liaoxi in Pingzhou, Shanggu in Yanzhou, and Yuyang in Youzhou, each with ten thousand households, bringing his total fief to one hundred thousand households. This became the domain of the State of Taiyuan, and he was further promoted to Grand Preceptor.
9
建義初，北海王元顥南奔梁，梁立為魏主，資以兵將。 時邢杲以三齊應顥。 朝廷以顥孤弱，永安二年春，詔元天穆先平齊地，然後征顥。 顥乘虛徑進，榮陽、武牢並不守，車駕出居河北。 榮聞之，馳傳朝行宮於上党之長子，輿駕於是南趣。 榮為前驅，旬日之間，兵馬大集。 天穆克平邢杲，亦度河以會。 車駕幸河內。 榮與顥相持於河上，無船不得即度。 議欲還北，更圖後舉。 黃門郎楊侃、高道穆等並固執以為不可。 屬馬渚諸楊雲有小船數艘，求為鄉導。 榮乃令都督尒硃兆等率精騎夜濟。 顥奔。 車駕度河，入居華林園。 詔加榮天柱大將軍，增封通前二十萬戶，加前後部羽葆鼓吹。
At the beginning of the Jianyi reign, the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, fled south to Liang. Liang installed him as ruler of Wei and supplied him with troops and generals. At that time Xing Gao rallied the Three Qi in support of Hao. The court considered Hao isolated and weak, and in the spring of the second year of Yong'an an edict ordered Yuan Tianmu first to pacify Qi territory and then march against Hao. Hao seized the opening and pressed straight forward. Rongyang and Wulao were both abandoned, and the imperial carriage withdrew north of the Yellow River. When Rong heard of this, he raced by post relay to attend the emperor at the traveling palace in Changzi in Shangdang, and the imperial carriage thereupon turned south. Rong served as vanguard, and within ten days troops and horses gathered in great force. Tianmu conquered and pacified Xing Gao and also crossed the river to join him. The emperor proceeded to Henei. Rong and Hao faced each other across the river, but without boats they could not cross immediately. In council some argued for returning north and planning a later campaign. Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yang Kan, Gao Daomu, and others all firmly insisted that this would not do. Just then Yang Yun of Mazhu had several small boats and offered to serve as guide. Rong then ordered the commander Erzhu Zhao and others to lead elite horsemen across the river by night. Hao fled. The emperor crossed the river and took up residence in Hualin Park. An edict promoted Rong to Grand General Who Is the Pillar of Heaven, increased his fief to a total of two hundred thousand households, and granted him feather-canopied processional guards and martial music before and behind.
10
榮尋還晉陽，遙制朝廷，親戚腹心，皆補要職，百僚朝廷動靜，莫不以申。 至於除授，皆須榮許，然後得用。 莊帝雖受制權臣，而勤政事，朝夕省納，孜孜不已。 數自理冤獄，親覽辭訟。 又選司多濫，與吏部尚書李神俊議正綱紀。 而榮乃大相嫌責。 曾關補定州曲陽縣令，神俊以階縣不奏，別更擬人。 榮大怒，即遣其所補者往奪其任。 榮使入京，雖復微蔑，朝貴見之，莫不傾靡。 及至闕下，未得通奏，恃榮威勢，至乃忿怒。 神俊遂上表遜位。 榮欲用世隆攝選，上亦不違。 榮曾啟北人為河內諸州，欲為掎角勢，上不即從。 天穆入見論事，上猶未許。 天穆曰：「天柱既有大功，為國宰相，若請普代天下官屬，恐陛下亦不得違。 如何啟數人為州，便停不用？ 」帝正色曰：「天柱若不為人臣，朕亦須代； 如其猶存臣節，無代天下百官理。 」榮聞，大怒曰：「天子由誰得立？ 今乃不用我！ 」語皇后復嫌內妃嬪甚有妒恨之事。 帝遣世隆語以大理，後曰：「天子由我家置立，今便如此。 我父本日即自作，今亦復決？ 」世隆曰：「兄止自不為，若本自作，臣今亦得封王。 」帝既外迫強臣，內逼皇后，恆怏怏不以萬乘為貴。
Rong soon returned to Jinyang and controlled the court from afar. Kinsmen and trusted intimates were all appointed to key posts, and every movement of officials at court had to be reported to him. As for appointments and dismissals, all required Rong's approval before they could take effect. Although Emperor Xiaozhuang was constrained by a powerful minister, he diligently attended to government affairs, reviewing matters morning and evening without cease. He repeatedly handled cases of wrongful imprisonment himself and personally examined petitions and lawsuits. Moreover, the selection offices were rife with abuse, and he discussed with the Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, Li Shenjun, how to restore proper standards. But Rong greatly resented this and reproached him for it. Once, when an appointment to the magistracy of Quyang County in Dingzhou came up for approval, Shenjun, considering the county too low in rank to warrant a memorial, separately nominated someone else. Rong was furious and immediately sent the man he had appointed to seize the post. When Rong's emissaries entered the capital, though they were men of low rank, every great official at court bowed before them. When they reached the palace gates and were not granted audience to memorialize, they grew angry, relying on Rong's power and prestige. Shenjun thereupon submitted a memorial resigning his post. Rong wished to have Shilong act as interim head of selection, and the emperor did not oppose it. Rong had once petitioned to appoint northerners to the provinces of the Henei region, wishing to form a pincer force, but the emperor did not immediately agree. When Tianmu entered audience to discuss the matter, the emperor still would not approve. Tianmu said: "The Pillar of Heaven has already rendered great service and serves as the state's chief minister. If he were to request replacing every official throughout the realm, I fear Your Majesty could not refuse either. How can you petition for a few men to be made provincial governors and then refuse to appoint them? " The emperor said sternly: "If the Pillar of Heaven is no longer to be a subject, then I too must be replaced; but if he still preserves the conduct of a subject, there is no reason to replace every official throughout the realm. " When Rong heard of this, he said in great anger: "By whom was the Son of Heaven able to ascend the throne? And now he will not heed me! " When he spoke with the empress, he again complained of the inner consorts and of many matters of jealousy and resentment. The emperor sent Shilong to reason with her, but the empress said: "The Son of Heaven was installed by our house, and now he acts like this. My father could have made himself ruler on that very day—will he decide to do so again now? " Shilong said: "My elder brother simply chose not to do so himself. Had he made himself ruler from the start, I too would now hold a princely title. " The emperor, pressed from without by a powerful minister and from within by the empress, was constantly discontent and did not regard the imperial throne as a blessing.
11
先是，葛榮枝党韓婁仍據幽、平二州，榮遣都督侯深討斬之。 時万俟醜奴、蕭寶夤擁眾豳、涇，榮遣其從子天光為雍州刺史，令率都督賀拔岳、侯莫陳悅等入關討之。 天光至雍州，以眾少未進。 榮大怒，遣其騎兵參軍劉貴馳驛詣軍，加天光杖罰。 天光等大懼，乃進討，連破之，禽醜奴、寶夤，並檻車送闕。 天光又禽王慶雲、万俟道樂，關中悉平。 於是天下大難便盡。 莊帝恆不慮外寇，唯恐榮為逆。 常時諸方未定，欲使與之相持。 及告捷之日，乃不甚喜，謂尚書令、臨淮王彧曰：「即今天下，便是無賊？ 」臨淮見帝色不悅，曰：「臣恐賊平以後，方勞聖慮。 」帝畏餘人怪，還以他語解之，曰：「其實撫甯荒余，彌成不易。」
Earlier, Han Lou, a remnant follower of Ge Rong, still held You and Ping provinces, and Rong sent the commander Hou Shen to campaign against and execute him. At that time Moqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin held large forces in Bin and Jing, and Rong sent his nephew Tianguang as Inspector of Yongzhou, ordering him to lead the commanders Heba Yue, Houmochen Yue, and others through the passes to campaign against them. When Tianguang reached Yongzhou, he did not advance because his force was too small. Rong was furious and sent his Cavalry Army Aide Liu Gui racing by post relay to the army to have Tianguang beaten. Tianguang and the others were terrified and then advanced to campaign, defeating the enemy in succession, capturing Chounu and Baoyin, and sending them both to the capital in caged carts. Tianguang also captured Wang Qingyun and Moqi Daole, and all of Guanzhong was pacified. Thereupon the great calamities afflicting the realm were at an end. Emperor Xiaozhuang constantly gave no thought to foreign enemies and feared only that Rong would rebel. While the various regions were still unsettled, he had wished to keep them locked in mutual contention with Rong. On the day victory was reported, he was not greatly pleased and said to the Minister-in-Chief, the Prince of Linhuai, Yuan Yu: "So now throughout the realm there are no more rebels? " When Linhuai saw that the emperor looked displeased, he said: "Your servant fears that after the rebels are pacified, Your Majesty's concerns will only then truly begin. " The emperor, fearing that others would find it strange, changed the subject and said: "In truth, to pacify and settle the devastated regions will be all the more difficult."
12
榮好射獵，不舍寒暑，法禁嚴重。 若一鹿出，乃有數人殞命。 曾有一人，見猛獸便走，謂曰：「欲求活邪！ 」遂即斬之。 自此獵如登戰場。 曾見一猛獸在窮穀中，乃令餘人重衣空手搏之，不令復損。 於是數人被殺，遂禽得之。 持此而樂焉。 列圍而進，雖阻險不得回避，其下甚苦之。
Rong loved hunting and archery and did not cease in cold or heat, and the regulations he enforced were severe. If a single deer appeared, several men might lose their lives. Once there was a man who, on seeing a fierce beast, ran away, and Rong said to him: "Do you wish to live? " He then immediately beheaded him. From then on, the hunt was waged like a battlefield. Once, when he spotted a fierce beast in a deep ravine, he ordered the others to don heavy clothing and wrestle it bare-handed, forbidding any further harm to the animal with weapons. Several men were killed in the struggle, but the beast was finally captured. He took delight in such sport. They formed a beat and drove forward; even where the terrain was treacherous they were forbidden to hang back, and his followers found it unbearable.
13
太宰元天穆從容言榮勳業，宜調政養人。 榮便攘肘謂天穆曰：「太后女主，不能自正，推奉天子者，此是人臣常節。 葛容之徒，本是奴才，乘時作亂，譬如奴走，禽獲便休。 頃來受國大寵，未能混一海內，何宜今日便言勳也？ 如聞朝士猶自寬縱，今秋欲共兄戒勒士馬，校獵嵩原，令貪汙朝貴，入圍搏虎。 仍出魯陽，曆三荊，悉擁生蠻，北填六鎮。 回軍之際，因平汾胡。 明年簡練精騎，分出江、淮，蕭衍若降，乞萬戶侯； 如其不降，徑度數千騎，便往縛取。 待六合寧一，八表無塵，然後共兄奉天子巡四方，觀風俗，布政教，如此乃可稱勳耳。 今若止獵，兵士懈怠，安可復用也？」
Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu calmly suggested that, given Rong's meritorious service, it was time to adjust governance and nurture the people. Rong then brushed him aside and said to Tianmu: "The empress dowager is a woman holding power and cannot set things right herself; to support and raise up the Son of Heaven is the ordinary duty of a minister. Men like Ge Rong were bondsmen to begin with; they seized the moment to rebel. Like a runaway slave, once captured the matter is over. We have only lately received the state's greatest favor, and we have not yet unified the realm—how can we speak of merit today? I hear court officials are still indulgent and lax. This autumn I wish to join my elder brother in drilling troops and horses and hunting on the Song Plain, forcing the corrupt court nobles into the beat to wrestle tigers. Then march out through Ruyang, pass through the Three Jings, drive all the unsubdued barbarians before us, and reinforce the Six Garrisons in the north. On the return march, we will pacify the Fen Hu as we go. Next year we will drill elite cavalry and send columns toward the Yangtze and Huai. If Xiao Yan submits, I ask for a marquisate of ten thousand households; if he does not submit, a few thousand cavalry will cross at once and go bind and capture him. When the six directions are at peace, the realm is unified, and the eight quarters are free of turmoil, then together with my elder brother we will escort the Son of Heaven on tour through the land, observe local customs, and spread government and teaching—only then may we speak of merit. If we stop hunting now, the soldiers will grow slack—how could they ever be used again?"
14
及見四方無事，乃遣人奏曰：「參軍許周勸臣取九錫，臣惡其此言，已發遣令去。 」榮時望得殊禮，故以意諷朝廷。 帝實不欲與之，因稱其忠。 榮見帝年長明悟，為眾所歸，欲移自近，皆使由己。 每因醉雲，入將天子，拜謁金陵後，還復恆朔。 而侍中硃元龍輒從尚書索太和中遷京故事，於是復有移都消息。
When he saw that the four quarters were at peace, he sent a memorial saying: "Army Aide Xu Zhou urged me to accept the Nine Distinctions. I detest such talk and have already dismissed him and sent him away. " Rong at the time hoped to receive extraordinary honors and used the memorial to obliquely prod the court. Emperor Xiaozhuang in truth did not wish to grant them and therefore praised his loyalty. Rong saw that Emperor Xiaozhuang was grown, clear-minded, and winning the allegiance of the people; he wished to move the capital nearer to himself and have everything pass through his hands. Each time, after he had drunk himself into a stupor, he would take the Son of Heaven in with him; after paying obeisance in the imperial precinct, they would return as before on the first of the month. Palace Attendant Zhu Yuanlong repeatedly asked the Masters of Writing for the precedents on moving the capital during the Tahe era, and rumors of a capital transfer arose once again.
15
榮乃暫來向京，言看皇后娩難。 帝懲河陰之事，終恐難保，乃與城陽王徽、侍中楊侃、李彧、尚書右僕射元羅謀，皆勸帝刺殺之。 唯膠東侯李侃晞、濟陰王暉業言榮若來，必有備，恐不可圖。 又欲殺其黨與，發兵拒之。 帝疑未定，而京師人懷憂懼，中書侍郎邢子才之徒，已避之東出。 榮乃遍與朝士書，相任留。 中書舍人溫子升以書呈帝，帝恆望其不來，及見書，以榮必來，色甚不悅。 武衛將軍奚毅，建義初往來通命，帝每期之甚重，然以為榮通親，不敢與之言情。 毅曰：「若必有變，臣甯死陛下難，不能事契胡。 」帝曰：「朕保天柱無異心，亦不忘卿忠款。」
Rong then came temporarily toward the capital, saying he wished to attend the empress during her difficult childbirth. Emperor Xiaozhuang, mindful of the He'yin massacre, ultimately feared he could not preserve himself. He plotted with the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, Palace Attendant Yang Kan, Li Yu, and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo, and all urged him to assassinate Rong. Only the Marquis of Jiaodong, Li Kanxi, and the Prince of Jiyin, Huiye, argued that if Rong came he would certainly be on his guard, and they feared the plot could not succeed. They also considered killing his followers and raising troops to resist him. Emperor Xiaozhuang hesitated and could not decide, but the people of the capital were gripped by fear; the Secretariat Gentleman Xing Zicai and others had already fled east to escape the coming crisis. Rong then wrote to court officials throughout the capital, urging one another to stay and keep faith. Secretariat Drafter Wen Zisheng presented the letter to Emperor Xiaozhuang, who had constantly hoped Rong would not come. When he saw the letter and knew Rong would certainly come, his face darkened. General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi had gone back and forth bearing communications at the beginning of the Jianyi era, and Emperor Xiaozhuang always placed great hope in him. Yet because he believed Yi was close to Rong, he did not dare confide the plan. Yi said: "If crisis must come, your servant would rather die in Your Majesty's cause than serve the Jie barbarians. " Emperor Xiaozhuang said: "We guarantee that the Pillar of Heaven harbors no disloyal intent, and We shall not forget your loyal devotion."
16
三年八月，榮將四五千騎，發并州向京。 時人皆言其反，復道天子必應圖之。 九月初，榮至京。 有人告雲，帝欲圖之。 榮即具奏。 帝曰：「外人亦言王欲害我，豈可信之？ 」於是榮不自疑，每入謁帝，從人不過數十，皆不持兵仗。 帝欲止，城陽王曰：「縱不反，亦何可耐？ 況何可保耶？ 」又北人語訛，語「尒硃」為「人主」。 上又聞其在北言，我姓人主。 先是，長星出中台，掃大角，恆州人高榮祖頗明天文，榮問之曰：「是何祥也？ 」答曰：「除舊佈新象也。 昔長星掃大角，秦以之亡。 」榮聞之悅。 又榮下行台郎中李顯和曾曰：「天柱至，那無九錫，安須王自索也？ 亦是天子不見機！ 」都督郭羅察曰：「今年真可作禪文，何但九錫。 」參軍褚光曰：「人言并州城上有紫氣，何慮天柱不應。 」榮下人皆陵侮帝左右，無所忌憚，其事皆上聞。 奚毅又見，求聞。 帝即下明光殿與語。 帝又疑其為榮，不告以情。 及知毅赤誠，乃召城陽王徽及楊侃、李彧，告以毅語。 榮小女嫁與帝兄子陳留王，小字伽邪。 榮嘗指之曰：「我終當得此女婿力。 」徽又云：「榮慮陛下終為此患，脫有東宮，必貪立孩幼。 若皇后不生太子，則立陳留以安天下。 」並言榮指陳留語狀。 帝既有圖榮意，夜夢手持一刀自害，落十指節，都不覺痛。 惡之，以告城陽王徽及楊侃。 徽解夢曰：「蝮蛇螫手，壯士解腕。 割指節與解腕何異？ 去患乃是吉祥。 」聞者皆言善。
In the eighth month of the third year, Rong led four or five thousand cavalry from Bingzhou toward the capital. People at the time all said he was rebelling, and again declared that the Son of Heaven would surely move to destroy him. At the beginning of the ninth month, Rong reached the capital. Someone reported that Emperor Xiaozhuang intended to destroy him. Rong immediately submitted a full memorial about it. Emperor Xiaozhuang said: "Outsiders also say the prince wishes to harm me—how can such talk be believed? " Thereupon Rong put aside his suspicions. Each time he entered audience with the emperor, he brought no more than several dozen followers, and none carried weapons. Emperor Xiaozhuang wished to abandon the plan, but the Prince of Chengyang said: "Even if he does not rebel, how can he be endured? And how can his loyalty be trusted? " Moreover, northern speech slurs words: they pronounce "Erzhu" as "ruler of men." The emperor also heard that in the north Rong had said, "My surname is Ruler of Men." Earlier a baleful star had appeared at the Central Terrace and swept through Great Horn. Gao Rongzu of Hengzhou, who was well versed in astronomy—Rong asked him: "What omen is this? " He answered: "It is the sign of removing the old and establishing the new. In former times, when a baleful star swept through Great Horn, Qin perished because of it. " Rong heard this and was pleased. Li Xianhe, a bureau aide under Rong's mobile headquarters, also once said: "When the Pillar of Heaven arrives, how could there be no Nine Distinctions—why must the prince ask for them himself? It is the Son of Heaven who fails to read the signs! " Commander Guo Luocha said: "This year one could truly compose an abdication document—why stop at the Nine Distinctions? " Army Aide Chu Guang said: "People say purple vapor rises above Bingzhou city—why worry that the Pillar of Heaven will not receive his due? " All of Rong's subordinates insulted and browbeat the emperor's attendants without restraint, and word of everything reached the emperor. Xi Yi had another audience and asked to speak privately. Emperor Xiaozhuang immediately went down to the Hall of Bright Light to speak with him. Emperor Xiaozhuang again suspected he was Rong's agent and did not confide the plan. When he learned of Yi's pure loyalty, he summoned the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, Yang Kan, and Li Yu and told them what Yi had said. Rong's younger daughter was married to the Chenliu Prince, son of the emperor's elder brother, whose childhood name was Jiaye. Rong once pointed to him and said: "I will ultimately have this son-in-law's strength behind me. " Hui further reported: "Rong fears that Your Majesty will ultimately become this threat. If there is a crown prince, he will greedily seek to install a young child instead. If the empress does not bear a crown prince, he would install Chenliu to settle the realm. " He also reported what Rong had said while pointing at Chenliu. Emperor Xiaozhuang, already intent on destroying Rong, dreamed one night that he held a knife and cut himself, severing the joints of all ten fingers, yet felt no pain at all. He found the dream ominous and told the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, and Yang Kan. Hui interpreted the dream: "When a viper bites the hand, the brave man severs his wrist. How is cutting off finger joints different from severing the wrist? Removing the affliction is itself auspicious. " All who heard said he had spoken well.
17
九月十五日，天穆到京，駕迎之。 榮與天穆並從入西林園燕射。 榮乃奏曰：「近來侍官皆不習武，陛下宜將五百騎出獵，因省辭訟。 」先是奚毅言榮因獵挾天子移都，至是，其言相符。 至十八日，召中書舍人溫子升告以殺榮狀，並問以殺董卓事。 子升具通本，上曰：「王允若即赦涼州人，必不應至此。 」良久，語子升曰：「朕之情理，卿所具知，死猶須為，況必不死！ 甯與高貴鄉公同日死，不與常道鄉公同日生。 」上謂殺榮、天穆，即赦其党，便應不動。 應詔王道習曰：「尒硃世隆、司馬子如、硃元龍比來偏被委付，具知天下虛實，謂不宜留。 」城陽王及楊侃曰：「若世隆不全，仲遠、天光豈有來理？ 」帝亦謂然，無復殺意。 城陽曰：「榮數征伐，腰間有刀，或能狠戾傷人。 臨事，願陛下出。 」乃伏侃等十餘人於明光殿東。 其日，榮與天穆併入，坐食未訖，起出。 侃等從東階上殿，見榮、天穆出至中庭，事不果。 十九日是帝忌日。 二十日榮忌日。 二十一日，暫入，即向陳留王家，飲酒極醉。 遂言病動，頻日不入。 上謀頗泄，世隆等以告榮。 榮輕帝，不謂能反。 預帝謀者皆懼。 二十五日旦，榮、天穆同入，其日大欲革易。 上在明光殿東序中西面坐，榮與天穆並御床西北小床上南坐，城陽入，始一拜。 榮見光祿卿魯安等持刀從東戶入，即馳向御坐，帝拔千牛刀，手斬之，時年三十八。 得其手板上有數牒啟，皆左右去留人名，非其腹心，悉在出限。 帝曰：「豎子！ 若過今日，便不可制。 」時又天穆與榮子菩提亦就戮，於是內外喜叫，聲滿京城。 既而大赦。
On the fifteenth day of the ninth month, Yuan Tianmu reached the capital, and the imperial carriage went out to meet him. Rong and Tianmu both followed in and entered the Western Grove Garden for a feast and archery contest. Rong then memorialized: "Recently the attendants are all untrained in martial arts. Your Majesty ought to take five hundred cavalry out hunting and thereby review legal cases. " Earlier Xi Yi had said Rong would use the hunt to take the Son of Heaven hostage and move the capital—now his words proved true. On the eighteenth day, he summoned Secretariat Drafter Wen Zisheng, told him the plan to kill Rong, and also asked him about the killing of Dong Zhuo. Zisheng related the whole story. Emperor Xiaozhuang said: "If Wang Yun had immediately pardoned the Liangzhou men, it would certainly not have come to this. " After a long silence, he said to Zisheng: "You know my feelings and reasoning full well. The deed must be done even if death is certain—and how much more when death is not! Better to die on the same day as the Duke of Gaogu District than to live on the same day as the Duke of Changdao District. " The emperor believed that if Rong and Tianmu were killed and their faction immediately pardoned, the realm would remain calm. Yingzhao Wang Daoxi said: "Erzhu Shilong, Sima Ziru, and Zhu Yuanlong have lately been especially entrusted with power; they know the realm's strengths and weaknesses through and through, and I say they should not be spared. " The Prince of Chengyang and Yang Kan said: "If Shilong is not kept alive and whole, what reason would Zhongyuan and Tianguang have to come? " Emperor Xiaozhuang agreed and no longer intended to kill them. The Prince of Chengyang said: "Rong has fought in many campaigns. He carries a knife at his waist and might turn violent and harm someone. When the moment comes, I ask that Your Majesty withdraw. " They then hid Kan and more than ten others east of the Hall of Bright Light. That day Rong and Tianmu entered together. They had not finished their meal when they rose and left. Kan and the others rushed up the eastern stairs, but saw Rong and Tianmu already out in the central courtyard—the attempt came to nothing. The nineteenth was the emperor's day of mourning. The twentieth was Rong's day of mourning. On the twenty-first, Rong briefly entered court, then went straight to the Chenliu princely house and drank until utterly drunk. He then claimed his old illness was flaring up and for several days did not enter court. The emperor's plot leaked badly, and Shilong and the others told Rong. Rong looked down on the emperor and did not think him capable of striking back. All who shared in the emperor's plot were terrified. On the morning of the twenty-fifth, Rong and Tianmu entered together—the day on which the great change was to be carried out. Emperor Xiaozhuang sat facing west in the western wing of the Hall of Bright Light's eastern gallery. Rong and Tianmu both sat facing south on low couches northwest of the imperial couch. When the Prince of Chengyang entered, he offered only a single bow. When Rong saw Grand Master of Splendor Lu An and others enter through the eastern gate with drawn blades, he rushed toward the imperial seat. Emperor Xiaozhuang drew his imperial sword and struck off his head with his own hand. Rong was thirty-eight years old. On his tally board were found several slips listing names of attendants to be dismissed or retained; all who were not his close intimates were marked for removal. Emperor Xiaozhuang said: "Vile whelp! If he had lived beyond today, he could no longer have been controlled. " At the same time Yuan Tianmu and Rong's son Puti were also executed. Joyous shouts erupted inside and outside the palace, filling the capital. Soon after, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
18
榮雖威名大振，而舉止輕脫，止以馳射為伎藝，每入朝見，更無所為，唯戲上下馬。 于西林園宴射，恆請皇后出觀，並召王公妃主，共在一堂。 每見天子射中，輒自起舞叫，將相卿士，悉皆盤旋，乃至妃主婦人，亦不免隨之舉袂。 及酒酣耳熱，必自匡坐，唱虜歌，為《樹梨普梨》之曲。 見臨淮王彧從容閒雅，愛尚風素，固令為敕勒舞。 日暮罷歸，便與左右聯手蹋地，唱《回波樂》而出。 性甚嚴暴，慍喜無恆，弓箭刀槊，不離於手，每有瞋嫌，即行忍害，左右恆有死憂。 曾欲出獵，有人訴之，披陳不已，發怒，即射殺之。 曾見沙彌重騎一馬，榮即令相觸，力窮不復能動，遂使傍人以頭相擊，死而後已。
Though Erzhu Rong's martial renown was immense, his bearing was frivolous and rash. Horsemanship and archery were his only real skills. Each time he entered court audience he did nothing of substance, only amused himself by mounting and dismounting his horse. At the Western Grove Park he held feasting and archery contests, constantly asking the empress to come out and watch, and summoning princes, dukes, imperial consorts, and princesses to gather in a single hall. Whenever he saw Emperor Xiaozhuang hit the target, he would leap up dancing and shouting. Generals, ministers, and grandees all spun about in turn, and even imperial consorts and court ladies could not help raising their sleeves and joining in. When the wine had gone to his head and flushed his ears, he would sit bolt upright and sing barbarian songs, performing the tune "Shuli Puli." Seeing Prince Linhuai Yu composed and refined, a man who loved plain elegance, Erzhu Rong insisted that he perform the Tiele dance. At day's end, when the gathering broke up and he went home, he would join hands with his attendants, stamp the ground in rhythm, and leave singing "Returning Waves." His nature was savagely violent, his moods utterly unpredictable. Bow, arrows, knife, and spear never left his hand. At the slightest grievance he would kill on the spot, and those around him lived in constant dread of death. Once, when he was about to go hunting, a man came to plead a case and would not stop presenting his grievance. Enraged, Erzhu Rong shot him dead on the spot. Once he saw a novice monk riding a heavily laden horse. Erzhu Rong ordered the horses to charge each other. When both beasts were spent and could no longer move, he had bystanders bash the riders' heads together until they were dead.
19
節閔帝初，世隆等得志，乃詔贈假黃鉞、相國、錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事、晉王，加九錫，給九旒鑾輅，武賁班劍三百人，轀輬車，准晉太宰、安平獻王故事，諡曰武。 又詔百官議榮配饗，司直劉季明曰：「晉王若配永安，則不能終臣節。 以此論之，無所配。 」世隆作色曰：「卿合配？ 」季明曰：「下官預在議限，據理而言，不合上心，誅翦唯命。 」眾為之危，季明自若。 世隆意不已，乃配享孝文廟庭。
At the beginning of the Jiemin Emperor's reign, after Erzhu Shilong and his faction had gained power, an edict posthumously invested Erzhu Rong with the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, the Chancellorship, the directorship of the Masters of Writing, supreme command over all armies at home and abroad, and the title Prince of Jin. He was granted the Nine Bestowments, the nine-tassel imperial carriage, three hundred guards bearing ceremonial swords, and an imperial hearse, following the precedent set for the Jin Grand Preceptor, the Prince of Anping. His posthumous title was Wu. Another edict ordered the officials to deliberate on pairing Erzhu Rong in the ancestral temple. Direct Censor Liu Jiming said: "If the Prince of Jin is paired with Yong'an, he cannot to the end fulfill the integrity of a loyal subject. Judging by that, there is no emperor with whom he may properly be paired. " Erzhu Shilong's expression darkened. "Would you be the one to pair with him? " Liu Jiming said: "I was included in this deliberation. I spoke according to reason. If that does not please you, I accept execution at your command." The assembly feared for him, but Liu Jiming remained perfectly composed. Erzhu Shilong was still not satisfied, and so had Erzhu Rong paired for worship in the court of Emperor Xiaowen's temple.
20
菩提位太常卿、開府儀同三司、侍中、特進。 死時年十四。 節閔帝初，加贈司徒，諡曰惠。
Bodhi held the posts of Grand Master of Ceremonies, Grand General with an independent office equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, and Special Advance. He was fourteen when he died. At the beginning of the Jiemin Emperor's reign, he was further posthumously granted Minister of Education. His posthumous title was Hui.
21
菩提弟叉羅，武衛將軍、梁郡王。 尋卒，贈司空公。
Bodhi's younger brother Chaluo was General of Martial Guards and Prince of Liang Commandery. He died soon after and was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
22
尒硃文暢
Erzhu Wenchang
23
尒硃文略
Erzhu Wenlue
24
弟文略，以兄叉羅卒無後，襲叉羅爵梁郡王。 文暢事當從坐，靜帝使人往晉陽，欲拉殺之。 神武特加寬貸，奏免之。 文略聰明俊爽，多所通習。 齊文襄嘗令章永興馬上彈琵琶，奏十餘曲，試使文略寫之，遂得八。 文襄戲之曰：「聰明人多不老壽，梁郡其慎之！ 」文略對曰：「命之修短，皆在明公。 」文襄愴然曰：「此不足慮。 」初，神武遣令恕文略十死，恃此益橫，多所陵忽。 齊天保末，嘗邀平秦、武興、汝南諸王至宅，供設奢麗，各有贈賄。 諸王共假聚寶物以要之，文略弊衣而往，從奴五十人，皆駿馬侯服。 其豪縱不遜如此。 平秦王有七百里馬，文略敵以好婢，賭取之。 明日，平秦王使人致請，文略殺馬及婢，以二銀器盛婢頭馬肉而遺之。 平秦王訴之于文宣，系於京畿獄。 文略彈琵琶，吹橫笛，謠詠倦極，便臥唱挽輓歌歌。 居數月，奪防者弓矢以射人，曰：「不然，天子不憶我。 」有司奏，遂伏法。 文略嘗大遺魏收金，請為父作佳傳，收論榮比韋、彭、伊、霍，蓋由是也。
The younger brother Erzhu Wenlue, because his elder brother Chaluo died without heirs, inherited Chaluo's title as Prince of Liang Commandery. Erzhu Wenchang was liable to joint punishment for the affair, and the Jing Emperor sent men to Jinyang intending to strangle him to death. Gao Huan specially granted him leniency and memorialized to have the sentence waived. Erzhu Wenlue was brilliant and quick-witted, broadly accomplished in many arts. Qi Wenxiang once had Zhang Yongxing play the pipa on horseback and perform more than ten pieces. He tested Erzhu Wenlue by having him transcribe them, and Wenlue reproduced eight. Wenxiang teased him, saying: "Clever men often do not live to old age. Prince of Liang Commandery, take care! " Erzhu Wenlue replied: "Whether life is long or short—all lies with Your Excellency." " Wenxiang said with sudden sadness: "That is nothing to worry about." Earlier, Gao Huan had left instructions to pardon Erzhu Wenlue ten times from death. Relying on this, Wenlue grew ever more overbearing and frequently insulted and slighted others. Near the end of the Qi Tianbao reign, he once invited the princes of Pingqin, Wuxing, and Runan to his residence, entertained them lavishly, and gave each gifts and bribes. The princes pooled borrowed treasures to impress him. Erzhu Wenlue arrived in shabby clothes, attended by fifty slaves on fine horses and dressed in princely garb. Such was the height of his arrogant insolence. The Prince of Pingqin owned a horse that could run seven hundred li in a day. Erzhu Wenlue wagered a fine maidservant against it and won the horse by gambling. The next day the Prince of Pingqin sent men to demand them back. Erzhu Wenlue slaughtered the horse and the maidservant, placed the maidservant's head and the horse's flesh in two silver vessels, and sent them to him. The Prince of Pingqin complained to Emperor Wenxuan, and Erzhu Wenlue was imprisoned in the capital prison. In prison Erzhu Wenlue played the pipa, blew the transverse flute, and sang ballads until utterly weary, then lay down and sang dirges. After several months he seized the guards' bow and arrows and shot at people, saying: "Otherwise the Son of Heaven will never remember me." The responsible officials memorialized, and he was executed. Erzhu Wenlue once gave Wei Shou a large gift of gold and asked him to write a fine biography of his father. Wei Shou's comparison of Erzhu Rong to Wei Zuo, Peng Zu, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang was probably because of this.
25
尒硃兆
Erzhu Zhao
26
兆字萬仁，榮從子也。 少善騎射，趫捷過人，數從榮遊獵，至窮岩絕澗，人所不能升降者，兆必先之。 手格猛獸，無所疑避。 榮以此特加賞愛，任為爪牙。 榮曾送台使，見二鹿，授兆二箭，令取供今食。 遂構火以待之。 俄而兆獲其一，榮欲誇使人，責兆不盡取，杖之五十。 榮之入洛，兆兼前鋒都督。 孝莊即位，封潁川郡公。 後從上党王天穆平邢杲。 又與賀拔勝擊斬元顥子冠受，禽之。 進破安豐王延明，顥乃退走。 莊帝還宮，論功除車騎大將軍、儀同三司、汾州刺史。
Erzhu Zhao, courtesy name Wanren, was Erzhu Rong's nephew. From youth Erzhu Zhao excelled at horsemanship and archery, swifter and more agile than any other man. He often accompanied Erzhu Rong on hunting excursions. At sheer cliffs and bottomless ravines where others could not go up or down, Zhao always went first. He grappled fierce beasts with his bare hands, never hesitating or shrinking. Erzhu Rong for this reason favored him all the more and employed him as his strong right hand. Once, while seeing off an envoy from the capital, Erzhu Rong saw two deer. He gave Erzhu Zhao two arrows and ordered him to bring them back for the day's meal. Erzhu Rong then built a fire and waited. Before long Erzhu Zhao brought back one. Wanting to boast before the envoy, Erzhu Rong blamed Zhao for not taking both and had him beaten fifty strokes. When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Erzhu Zhao also served as vanguard commander. When Emperor Xiaozhuang acceded, Erzhu Zhao was enfeoffed as Duke of Yingchuan Commandery. Later he followed the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, in pacifying the rebel Xing Gao. He also joined Heba Sheng in defeating and capturing Guanshou, son of Yuan Hao. Advancing further, he defeated the Prince of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming, and Yuan Hao then withdrew in flight. When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Erzhu Zhao was rewarded with appointment as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand General with an independent office equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Fenzhou.
27
尒硃榮死，兆自汾州據晉陽。 元曄立，授兆大將軍，進爵為王。 兆與世隆等定謀攻洛。 兆遂輕兵倍道，掩襲京邑。 先是，河邊人夢神謂己曰：「尒硃家欲度河，用爾作灅波津令，為之縮水脈。 」月餘，夢者死。 及兆至，有行人自言知水淺處，以草往往表插而導焉，忽失其所在。 兆遂策馬涉度。 是日暴風鼓怒，黃塵張天，騎叩宮門，宿衛乃覺。 彎弓欲射，袍撥弦，矢不得發，一時散走。 莊帝步出雲龍門外，為兆騎所擊，幽于永寧佛寺。 兆撲殺皇子，汙辱妃嬪，縱兵虜掠。 停洛旬余，先令衛送莊帝于晉陽，兆後於河梁監閱財貨。
After Erzhu Rong died, Erzhu Zhao seized Jinyang from his base in Fenzhou. When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Erzhu Zhao was granted the title Grand General and advanced in rank to prince. Erzhu Zhao joined Erzhu Shilong and the others in a plan to attack Luoyang. Erzhu Zhao then led light troops at forced march and made a surprise attack on the capital. Earlier, a man living by the river dreamed that a god said to him: "The Erzhu family wishes to cross the river. They will use you as magistrate of Luobo Ford to shrink the water's course for them. A little more than a month later, the dreamer died. When Erzhu Zhao arrived, a traveler claimed to know where the water was shallow. He marked the way by sticking tufts of grass here and there to guide them, then suddenly vanished without trace. Erzhu Zhao then spurred his horse and waded across. That day a violent wind roared and yellow dust filled the sky. Horsemen knocked on the palace gates before the palace guards even realized what was happening. They bent their bows to shoot, but their robes caught the bowstrings and the arrows would not fly. In an instant they scattered and fled. Emperor Xiaozhuang walked out beyond the Cloud Dragon Gate, was seized by Erzhu Zhao's horsemen, and confined in Yongning Buddhist Temple. Erzhu Zhao beat imperial princes to death, violated imperial consorts, and let his troops plunder the city. He remained in Luoyang for more than ten days. First he ordered guards to escort Emperor Xiaozhuang to Jinyang, while Erzhu Zhao himself stayed behind at the River Bridge to supervise the plunder.
28
初，兆將入洛，遣使招齊神武，欲與同舉。 神武時為晉州刺史，謂長史孫騰曰：「臣而伐君，其逆已甚。 我今不往，恐彼致恨，卿可往申吾意，但雲山蜀未平，不可委去。 」騰乃詣兆，具申意。 兆不悅，曰：「還白高兄弟，有吉夢，今行必克。 吾比夢吾亡父登一高堆，堆傍地悉耕熟，唯有馬蘭草株，往往猶在，吾父顧我，令下拔之。 吾手所至，無不盡出。 以此而言，往必有利。 」騰還，具報之。 神武曰：「兆等倡狂，舉兵犯順，吾勢不可反事尒硃也。 今天子列兵河上，兆進不能度，必退還。 吾乘山東下，出其不意，此徒可一舉而禽。 」俄而兆克京師，孝莊幽縶，都督尉景從兆南行，以書報神武。 神武大驚，召騰，令馳驛詣兆，示以謁賀，密觀天子所在，當于路邀迎，唱大義於天下。 騰遇帝于中路，神武時率騎東轉，聞帝已度，於是西還。 仍與兆書，具陳禍福，不宜害天子，受惡名於海內。 兆怒不納，而帝遂遇弑。
Earlier, when Erzhu Zhao was about to enter Luoyang, he sent envoys to summon Gao Huan, wishing to rise together with him. Gao Huan was then Governor of Jinzhou. He said to Chief Clerk Sun Teng: "A subject attacking his ruler—that rebellion is already extreme. If I do not go now, I fear they will resent me. You may go and explain my intent, saying only that the mountains of Shu are not yet pacified and I cannot leave my post. Sun Teng then went to Erzhu Zhao and fully explained Gao Huan's intent. Erzhu Zhao was displeased and said: "Go back and tell Brother Gao: I had an auspicious dream. If I march now, I am certain to prevail. Recently I dreamed that my dead father climbed a high mound. The ground beside the mound was all plowed and ripe, yet stalks of horse orchid grass still stood here and there. My father looked back at me and ordered me to go down and pull them up. Wherever my hand reached, every stalk came out by the roots. By that omen, the march is sure to succeed. Sun Teng returned and reported all of this to Gao Huan. Gao Huan said: "Zhao and the others are wildly reckless, raising troops in violation of right order. For me, there can be no turning back to serve the Erzhu clan. The Son of Heaven has arrayed troops on the river. If Zhao advances and cannot cross, he is certain to withdraw. I will ride down from the eastern mountains and take them unawares. That band can be captured in a single stroke. Before long Erzhu Zhao took the capital. Emperor Xiaozhuang was imprisoned. Commander Wei Jing followed Zhao south and reported by letter to Gao Huan. Gao Huan was greatly alarmed. He summoned Sun Teng and ordered him to ride post-haste to Erzhu Zhao, feign congratulations, secretly learn where the emperor was, intercept and welcome him on the road, and proclaim righteousness to the realm. Sun Teng met the emperor midway. Gao Huan was then leading his horsemen eastward, but hearing that the emperor had already passed, he turned back west. He then wrote to Erzhu Zhao, fully setting forth the consequences, urging that he must not harm the Son of Heaven and incur infamy throughout the realm. Erzhu Zhao angrily refused, and the emperor was then assassinated.
29
初，榮既死，莊帝詔河西人紇豆陵步蕃等，令襲秀容。 兆入洛後，步蕃兵勢甚盛，南逼晉陽。 兆所以不暇留洛，回師禦之。 頻為步蕃所敗，於是部勒士馬，謀出山東，令人頻徵神武。 神武晉州僚屬，並勸不行。 神武揣其勢迫，必無他慮，決策赴之。 兆乃分三州六鎮之人，令神武統領。 神武既分兵別營，乃引兵南出，避步蕃之銳。 步蕃至樂平郡，神武與兆還討，破斬之。 及節閔帝立，授兆使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、柱國大將軍，兼錄尚書事、大行台。 又以兆為天柱大將軍，兆以是榮所終之官，固辭不拜。 尋加都督十州諸軍事，世襲并州刺史。
Earlier, after Erzhu Rong died, Emperor Xiaozhuang ordered the Hexi commander Qidouling Bufan and others to attack Xiurong. After Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Bufan's army grew very powerful and pressed south toward Jinyang. That was why Erzhu Zhao could not linger in Luoyang and turned his army back to resist him. Repeatedly defeated by Bufan, he reorganized his troops and planned to move out toward the eastern mountains, sending men repeatedly to summon Gao Huan. All of Gao Huan's staff in Jinzhou urged him not to go. Gao Huan reckoned that with their situation desperate, they would certainly have no other designs, and decided to go. Erzhu Zhao then placed the people of three provinces and six garrisons under Gao Huan's command. Once Gao Huan had divided his troops into separate camps, he led his army south, avoiding Bufan's main force. When Bufan reached Leping Commandery, Gao Huan and Erzhu Zhao turned back to attack him, defeated him, and beheaded him. When the Jiemin Emperor was enthroned, Erzhu Zhao was granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, supreme command over all armies at home and abroad, Pillar of State Grand General, and concurrent Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner. Erzhu Zhao was also offered the title Pillar of Heaven Grand General, but because that was the last office Erzhu Rong had held, Zhao firmly declined. Soon he was further granted command over the armies of ten provinces, with hereditary succession as Governor of Bingzhou.
30
神武之克殷州也，兆與仲遠、度律約拒之。 仲遠、度律次陽平，兆屯廣阿，眾號十萬。 神武廣縱反間，於是兩不相信，各致猜疑。 仲遠等頻使斛斯椿賀拔勝往喻之。 兆輕騎三百，來就仲遠，同坐幕下。 兆性粗獷，意色不平，手舞馬鞭，長嘯凝望，深疑仲遠等有變，遂趨出馳還。 仲遠遣椿、勝等追而曉譬，兆遂拘縛將還，經日放遣。 仲遠等於是奔退。 神武乃進擊，兆軍大敗。 兆與仲遠、度律遂相疑阻，久而不和。 世隆請節閔納兆女為皇后，兆乃大喜。 世隆謀抗神武，乃降辭厚禮，喻兆赴洛。 兆與天光、度律更自信約，然後大會韓陵山。 戰敗，復奔晉陽。 其年秋，神武自鄴進討之，兆遂大掠并州，走于秀容。 神武又追擊，度赤洪嶺，破之。 兆竄於窮山，殺所乘馬，自縊於樹。 神武收葬之。
When Gao Huan took Yinzhou, Erzhu Zhao joined Zhongyuan and Dulu in an agreement to resist him. Zhongyuan and Dulu encamped at Yangping, Erzhu Zhao stationed his troops at Guang'a, and their combined forces were said to number one hundred thousand. Gao Huan spread disinformation widely, and the two sides lost trust in each other, each growing suspicious of the other. Zhongyuan and his allies repeatedly dispatched Husi Chun and Heba Sheng to reason with him. Erzhu Zhao rode in with three hundred light cavalry to meet Zhongyuan, and the two sat together under the command tent. Erzhu Zhao was coarse and volatile by nature. His face dark with suspicion, he flourished his riding crop, gave a long whistle, and stared into the distance, convinced that Zhongyuan and the others meant to turn on him. He bolted from the tent and galloped away. Zhongyuan sent Husi Chun, Heba Sheng, and others in pursuit to reason with him. Erzhu Zhao was seized, bound, and brought back, then released and sent off a day later. Zhongyuan and his forces thereupon broke and fled. Gao Huan then pressed the attack, and Erzhu Zhao's army was routed. Erzhu Zhao, Zhongyuan, and Dulu grew mutually suspicious and obstructive, and remained at odds for a long time. Erzhu Shilong persuaded the Jiemin Emperor to take Erzhu Zhao's daughter as empress, and Zhao was overjoyed. Erzhu Shilong plotted to resist Gao Huan and sent humble messages and lavish gifts to coax Erzhu Zhao to Luoyang. Erzhu Zhao, Erzhu Tianguang, and Dulu reaffirmed their alliance, then mustered their full strength at Hanling Mountain. They were defeated in battle and again fled to Jinyang. That autumn Gao Huan marched from Ye to attack him. Erzhu Zhao plundered Bingzhou on a vast scale and fled to Xiurong. Gao Huan pressed the pursuit again, crossed Red Hong Ridge, and broke his force. Erzhu Zhao hid in a desolate mountain, killed his mount, and hanged himself from a tree. Gao Huan recovered his body and gave him a proper burial.
31
兆勇於戰鬥，而無將領之能。 榮雖奇其膽決，然每云：「兆不過將三千騎，多則亂矣。」
Erzhu Zhao was fearless in combat but lacked the talent of a general. Erzhu Rong admired his boldness, yet always said, "Zhao can lead no more than three thousand horsemen; give him more and everything falls apart."
32
兆弟智彪，節閔帝封為安定王。 與兆俱走，神武禽之。 後死于晉陽。
Erzhu Zhao's younger brother Zhibiao was enfeoffed by the Jiemin Emperor as Prince of Anding. He fled together with Erzhu Zhao and was captured by Gao Huan. He later died at Jinyang.
33
尒硃彥伯
Erzhu Yanbo
34
彥伯，榮從弟也。 祖侯真，文成時並、安二州刺史、始昌侯。 父買珍，宣武時武衛將軍、華州刺史。
Erzhu Yanbo was Erzhu Rong's paternal cousin. His grandfather Hou Zhen had served under Emperor Wencheng as Inspector of Bing and An prefectures and as Marquis of Shichang. His father Mai Zhen had served under Emperor Xuanwu as General of the Military Guard and Inspector of Huazhou.
35
彥伯性和厚，永安中，為榮府長史。 節閔帝潛嘿于龍花佛寺，彥伯敦喻往來，尤有勤款。 帝既立，尒硃兆以己不豫謀，大為忿恚，將攻世隆。 詔令華山王鷙慰兆，兆猶不釋。 世隆復令彥伯自往喻之，兆乃止。 及還，帝宴彥伯于顯陽殿。 時侍中源子恭、黃門郎竇瑗並侍坐。 彥伯曰：「源侍中比為都督，與臣相持於河內。 當爾之時，旗鼓相望，眇如天隔。 甯期同事陛下，為今日之忻也？ 」子恭曰：「蒯通有言，犬吠非其主。 他日之事永安，猶今日之事陛下耳。 」帝曰：「源侍中可謂有射鉤之心也。 」遂令二人極醉而罷。 後封博陵郡王，位司徒公。 于時炎旱，有勸彥伯解司徒者，乃上表遜位，詔許之。 俄除儀同三司、侍中，餘如故。 彥伯于兄弟之中，差無過患。 天光等敗于韓陵，彥伯欲領兵屯河橋，世隆不從。 及張勸等掩襲世隆，彥伯時在禁直。 長孫承業等啟陳，神武義功既振，將除尒硃。 節閔令舍人郭崇報彥伯知，彥伯狼狽出走，為人所執。 尋與世隆同斬於閶闔門外，縣首於斛斯椿門樹，傳于神武。 先是洛中謠曰：「三月末，四月初，揚灰簸土覓真珠。 」又曰：「頭去項，腳根齊，驅上樹，不須梯。 」至是並驗。 子敞。
Erzhu Yanbo was mild and generous by nature. During the Yong'an era he served as chief clerk in Erzhu Rong's princely establishment. While the future Jiemin Emperor lived in silent seclusion at Longhua Buddhist Temple, Erzhu Yanbo went back and forth urging and explaining matters to him with exceptional earnest devotion. Once the emperor had been enthroned, Erzhu Zhao, furious that he had not been included in the plot, intended to attack Erzhu Shilong. An edict ordered Prince Hua of Huashan to placate Erzhu Zhao, but Zhao still would not be appeased. Erzhu Shilong again sent Erzhu Yanbo in person to reason with him, and Erzhu Zhao then desisted. When Yanbo returned, the Jiemin Emperor gave him a banquet in the Hall of Xianyang. Palace Attendant Yuan Zigong and Yellow Gate Gentleman Dou Yuan were both in attendance. Erzhu Yanbo said, "Attendant Yuan, you recently served as area commander and faced me in stalemate at Henei. In those days our banners and drums faced each other across the field, as though heaven itself lay between us. Who could have dreamed we would serve the same sovereign and share today's joy? " Yuan Zigong said, "Kuai Tong once said that a dog barks not for its proper master. What I did then in the service of Yong'an is what I do today in the service of Your Majesty. " The Jiemin Emperor said, "Attendant Yuan may truly be said to have the heart that forgave the hook-shooter." " He then had the two of them drink until utterly drunk, and the banquet ended. Later he was enfeoffed as Prince of Boling commandery and appointed Minister over the Masses. At that time a severe drought afflicted the land. Some urged Erzhu Yanbo to resign as Minister over the Masses; he submitted a memorial yielding his post, and an edict approved it. Soon he was appointed Yitong Sanqi and Palace Attendant; his other privileges remained unchanged. Among the Erzhu brothers, Yanbo was comparatively free of serious faults. When Erzhu Tianguang and the others were defeated at Hanling, Erzhu Yanbo wished to lead troops to hold the Heqiao Bridge, but Erzhu Shilong would not agree. When Zhang Qu and the others launched a surprise attack on Erzhu Shilong, Erzhu Yanbo was on night duty in the palace. Changsun Chenye and the others submitted a memorial stating that Gao Huan's righteous cause had already gained momentum and that he intended to eliminate the Erzhu clan. The Jiemin Emperor ordered Attendant-of-the-Interior Guo Chong to warn Erzhu Yanbo. Yanbo fled in disarray and was seized. Soon he was beheaded together with Erzhu Shilong outside the Changhe Gate. His head was hung on the gate-tree at Husi Chun's residence and sent on to Gao Huan. Earlier a song in Luoyang had run: "At the end of the third month, in the early fourth month, winnow ash and sift dust searching for true pearls. " Another ran: "Head severed from the neck, feet level with the roots—drive him up a tree, no ladder needed." " When the time came, both prophecies were fulfilled. His son was Erzhu Chang.
36
尒硃敞
Erzhu Chang
37
敞字乾羅。 彥伯之誅，敞小，隨母養于宮中。 年十二，敞自竇走至大街，見童兒群戲，敞解所著綺羅金翠服，易衣而遁。 追騎至，不識敞，便執綺衣兒。 比究問知非，會日已暮，由是免。 遂入一村，見長孫氏媼，踞胡床坐，敞再拜求哀，長孫氏湣之，藏於復壁之中。 購之愈急，追且至，長孫氏資而遣之。 遂詐為道士，變姓名，隱嵩高山。 略涉經史。 數年間，人頗異之。 嘗獨坐岩石下，泫然歎曰：「吾豈終此乎！ 伍子胥獨何人也？ 」乃奔長安。 周文帝見而禮之，拜行台郎中、靈壽縣伯。 保定中，遷開府儀同三司，進爵為公。 後為膠州刺史。 迎長孫氏至其第，置於家，厚資給之。 隋文帝受禪，改封邊城郡公。 黔安蠻叛，命敞討平之。 師旋，拜金州總管，政號嚴明，吏人懼之。 後以年老乞骸骨，賜二馬輅車歸河內，卒於家。 子最嗣。
Erzhu Chang's style name was Qianluo. When Erzhu Yanbo was executed, Chang was still a child and was raised in the palace with his mother. At twelve, Chang slipped through a hole in the wall to the main street. Seeing a group of children at play, he stripped off his brocade silks and gold-emerald finery, traded clothes with one of them, and fled. Pursuers arrived but did not recognize Chang; they seized the child in the brocade garments instead. When interrogation showed they had the wrong child, night had already fallen, and so Chang escaped capture. He entered a village and found an old woman of the Changsun clan seated on a folding chair. Chang bowed twice in supplication; she took pity on him and hid him in a concealed alcove. The manhunt grew fiercer and pursuers were nearly upon them. The Changsun woman gave him supplies and sent him on his way. He then passed himself off as a Daoist priest, changed his name, and hid on Mount Song. He dabbled in the classics and histories. Over several years people found him rather unusual. Once, sitting alone beneath a rock, he wept and sighed, "Am I to end my days like this! What made Wu Zixu so special? " He then fled to Chang'an. Emperor Wen of Zhou received him with honor and appointed him Langzhong of the mobile cabinet and Baron of Lingshou County. During the Baoding era he was promoted to Kaifu Yitong Sanqi and raised to the rank of duke. Later he served as Inspector of Jiaozhou. He brought the Changsun woman to his residence, housed her in his home, and supported her generously. When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Chang's fief was changed to Duke of Biancheng commandery. When the Qian'an tribes rebelled, he was ordered to suppress and pacify them. When his army returned he was appointed Governor-General of Jinzhou. His governance was strict and clear, and officials and commoners alike feared him. Later, citing old age, he requested retirement. He was granted a two-horse carriage, returned to Henei, and died at home. His son Zui succeeded him.
38
尒硃仲遠
Erzhu Zhongyuan
39
仲遠，彥伯弟也。 明帝末年，尒硃榮兵威稍盛，諸有啟謁，率多見從。 而仲遠摹寫榮書，又刻榮印，與尚書令吏，通為奸詐。 造榮啟表，請人為官，大得財貨，以資酒色。 落魄無行業。 及孝莊即位，封清河公、徐州刺史，兼尚書左僕射、三徐大行台。 尋進督三徐諸軍事。 仲遠上言：「竊見比來行台采募者，皆得權立中正，在軍定第，斟酌授官。 今求兼置，權濟軍要。 若立第亦爽，關京之日，任有司裁奪」。 詔從之。 於是隨情補授，肆意聚斂。
Zhongyuan was Erzhu Yanbo's younger brother. In the last years of Emperor Ming, Erzhu Rong's military power steadily grew, and most petitions and requests were granted. Zhongyuan copied Erzhu Rong's letters and carved a seal in Rong's name, colluding with clerks of the Masters of Writing in fraud. He forged memorials in Rong's name to procure offices for people, amassing great wealth to fund wine and women. He was dissolute and without proper conduct. When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe, appointed Inspector of Xuzhou, and concurrently made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Mobile Corps Commander of the Three Xus. Soon he was promoted to oversee all military affairs of the Three Xus. Zhongyuan submitted a memorial: "I observe that recently those recruiting troops through mobile corps have all been allowed to appoint local rankers on their own authority, fix grades within the army, and assign offices at discretion. I now request the same authority for myself, as a temporary measure to meet urgent military needs. If the grades I assign prove unsatisfactory, when the matter reaches the capital the responsible offices may revise them." An edict approved the request. He thereupon sold offices as he pleased and extorted wealth without restraint.
40
尒硃榮死，仲遠勒其部眾，來向京師。 節閔立，進爵彭城王，加大將軍，又兼尚書令，鎮大梁。 仲遠遣使請准朝式，在軍鳴騶。 節閔帝覽啟，笑而許之。 其肆情如此。 復進督東道諸軍事、本將軍、袞州刺史，余如故。 仲遠天性貪暴，心如峻壑。 大宗富族，誣之以反，沒其家口，簿籍財物，皆以入己。 丈夫死者，投之河流，如此者不可勝數。 諸將婦有美色者，莫不被其淫亂。 自滎陽以東，輸稅悉入其軍，不送京師。 時天光控關右，仲遠在大梁，兆據并州，世隆居京邑，各自專恣，權強莫此。 所在並以貪虐為事，於是四方解體。 又加太宰，解大行台。 仲遠專恣尤劇，方之彥伯、世隆，最為無禮。 東南牧守，下至人俗，比之豺狼，特為患苦。 後移屯東郡，率眾與度律等拒齊神武。 尒硃兆領騎數千自晉陽來會。 軍次陽平，神武縱以間說，仲遠等迭相猜貳，狼狽遁走。 中興二年，復與天光等於韓陵戰敗，南走。 尋乃奔梁，死於江南。
When Erzhu Rong died, Zhongyuan drove his troops toward the capital. When the Jiemin Emperor was enthroned, Zhongyuan was advanced to Prince of Pengcheng, given the title Grand General, made Director of the Masters of Writing, and stationed at Daliang. Zhongyuan sent envoys requesting permission to follow court protocol and have outriders announce his passage even while in the field. The Jiemin Emperor read the memorial, smiled, and granted it. Such was the extent of his self-indulgence. He was further promoted to oversee all military affairs of the Eastern Route, retained his original generalship, and was made Inspector of Yanzhou; his other offices remained unchanged. Zhongyuan was greedy and violent by nature; his heart was like a bottomless ravine. He falsely accused great clans and wealthy families of rebellion, confiscated their households, and recorded their goods and property—all for his own possession. Men who died were thrown into the river; such cases were beyond counting. No beautiful wife among the generals escaped his debauchery. From Xingyang eastward, all tax deliveries went into his army and never reached the capital. At the time Erzhu Tianguang controlled the lands west of the passes, Zhongyuan held Daliang, Erzhu Zhao held Bingzhou, and Erzhu Shilong dwelt in the capital. Each ruled with unchecked will, and none wielded power more absolutely. Everywhere they made greed and cruelty their business, and the realm began to fall apart on every side. He was further promoted to Grand Steward and stripped of his Grand Commandery Office. Erzhu Zhongyuan was the most unrestrained of the Erzhu clan—more arrogant and insolent even than Erzhu Yanbo and Erzhu Shilong. From the governors of the southeast down to ordinary people, all compared him to wolves and jackals; he was a singular affliction. He later shifted his camp to Dong commandery and led his forces with Erzhu Dulu and others to resist Gao Huan. Erzhu Zhao rode in from Jinyang with several thousand cavalry to join the coalition. When the army halted at Yangping, Gao Huan sent agents to spread dissension. Erzhu Zhongyuan and his allies turned on one another in suspicion and fled in disarray. In the second year of Zhongxing he was defeated again with Erzhu Tianguang and the others at Hanling and fled south. He soon fled to Liang and died in Jiangnan.

尒硃世隆
Erzhu Shilong
42
世隆，字榮宗，仲遠弟也。 明帝末，兼直閣，加前將軍。 尒硃榮表請入朝，靈太后惡之，令世隆詣晉陽慰喻榮。 榮因欲留之，世隆曰：「朝廷疑兄，故令世隆來。 今遂住，便有內備，非計之善。 」榮乃遣入。 榮舉兵南出，世隆遂走，會榮於上黨。 建義初，除給事黃門侍郎。 莊帝之立，世隆預其謀，封樂平郡公。 元顥逼大梁，詔為前將軍、都督，鎮武牢。 顥既克滎陽，世隆懼而遁還，莊帝倉卒北巡。 及車駕還宮，除尚書左僕射，攝選。
Erzhu Shilong, whose style name was Rongzong, was Erzhu Zhongyuan's younger brother. In the final years of Emperor Ming's reign he served concurrently in the palace attendants corps and was appointed Forward General. When Erzhu Rong petitioned to enter the capital, Empress Dowager Ling was hostile to the idea and ordered Erzhu Shilong to Jinyang to reassure him. Erzhu Rong wanted to keep him there. Shilong said, "The court suspects my brother, and that is why they sent me. If I remain, the court will take defensive measures at once. That would be a poor strategy. Erzhu Rong then let him proceed to the capital. When Erzhu Rong marched south at the head of his army, Shilong fled the capital and joined him at Shangdang. At the start of the Jianyi era he was appointed Chief of the Yellow Gate Attendants. When Emperor Xiaozhuang was enthroned, Shilong had taken part in the conspiracy and was enfeoffed as Duke of Leping commandery. When Yuan Hao threatened Daliang, an edict appointed Shilong Forward General and Area Commander with orders to hold Wu Fort. After Yuan Hao captured Xingyang, Shilong fled in panic, and Emperor Xiaozhuang made a hurried northern retreat. When the emperor returned to the palace, Shilong was appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat with acting authority over personnel appointments.
43
莊帝之將圖尒硃榮，每屏人言。 世隆懼變，乃為匿名書，自榜其門曰：「天子與侍中楊侃、黃門高道穆等為計，欲殺天柱。 」還復自以此書與榮妻北鄉郡公主，並以呈榮，勸其不入。 榮毀書唾地曰：「世隆無膽，誰敢生心！ 」世隆又勸其速發。 榮曰：「何忽忽？ 」皆不見從。
As Emperor Xiaozhuang plotted against Erzhu Rong, he would dismiss everyone from the room before speaking. Fearing a coup, Shilong wrote an anonymous warning and posted it on his own gate: "The emperor, Attendant-in-Ordinary Yang Kan, Huangmen Attendant Gao Daomu, and others are plotting to kill the Heavenly Pillar. He also sent the letter to Erzhu Rong's wife, the Princess of Beixiang commandery, and forwarded it to Rong himself, urging him not to enter the capital. Erzhu Rong tore the letter to pieces and spat on the ground. "Shilong hasn't the nerve for this—who would dare raise a hand against me? Shilong again urged him to leave at once. Erzhu Rong replied, "What's the hurry? He ignored every warning.
44
榮死，世隆奉榮妻，燒西陽門夜走。 北次河橋，殺武衛將軍奚毅，率眾還戰大夏門外。 及李苗燒絕河梁，世隆乃北遁。 攻建州克之，盡殺人以肆其忿。 至長子，與度律等共推長廣王曄為主。 曄小名盆子，聞者皆以為事類赤眉。 曄以世隆為尚書令，封樂平郡王，加太傅，行司州牧，會兆于河陽。 兆既平京邑，讓世隆曰：「叔父在朝多時，耳目應廣，如何令天柱受禍？ 」按劍嗔目，詞色甚厲。 世隆遜辭拜謝，然後得已，而深恨之。
After Erzhu Rong's death, Shilong escorted Rong's wife, set fire to the Western Yang Gate, and fled under cover of night. He halted at River Bridge to the north, killed General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi, and led his troops back to fight outside the Great Summer Gate. When Li Miao burned and destroyed the river bridge, Shilong fled north. He attacked and captured Jian province, slaughtering the population to vent his fury. At Changzi he joined Erzhu Dulu and the others in setting up Prince Guang of Chang as their sovereign. Ye's childhood name was Penzi—Basin-son—and everyone who heard it thought the episode recalled the Red Eyebrows rebellion. Ye made Shilong Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enfeoffed him as Prince of Leping commandery, appointed him Grand Tutor and acting Governor of Si province, and joined Erzhu Zhao at Heyang. Once Erzhu Zhao had pacified the capital, he upbraided Shilong: "Uncle, you spent years at court with eyes and ears everywhere—how could you let the Heavenly Pillar come to harm? Hand on his sword, eyes blazing, he spoke in a voice of fury. Shilong bowed and pleaded for mercy until Zhao relented, but he never forgave the humiliation.

時仲遠亦自滑台入京。 世隆與兄弟密謀，慮元曄母幹豫朝政，伺其母衛氏出行，遣數十騎如劫賊，於京巷殺之。 公私驚愕，莫識所由。 尋縣榜，以千萬錢募賊。 百姓知之，莫不喪氣。 尋又以曄疏遠，欲推立節閔帝。 而度律意在南陽王，乃曰：「廣陵不言，何以主天下？ 」後知能語，遂行廢立。
About this time Erzhu Zhongyuan also entered the capital from Huatai. Shilong and his brothers plotted in secret, fearing that Ye's mother would meddle in affairs of state. When Lady Wei, Ye's mother, went out, they sent several dozen horsemen disguised as bandits to kill her in a capital street. Officials and commoners alike were stunned; no one knew who had done it. Soon a public notice was posted offering ten million cash for the capture of the killers. When the people realized what had happened, their spirits sank. Finding Ye too remote and powerless, they soon moved to install the Jiemin Emperor instead. But Erzhu Dulu favored the Prince of Nanyang and objected: "Guangling cannot speak—how can he rule the realm? When they learned that Guangling could in fact speak, they proceeded with the deposition and enthronement.
