初，世隆之為僕射，尚書文簿，在家省閱。 性聰解，又畏榮，深自克勉，留心几案，傍接賓客，遂有解了之名。 榮死之後，無所顧憚。 及為令，常使尚書郎宋游道、邢昕在其宅聽事，東西別座，受納訴訟，稱命施行。 既總朝政，生殺自由，公行淫泆，信任群小，隨情與奪。 又兄弟群從，各擁強兵，割剝四海，極其貪虐。 奸諂蛆酷，多見信用； 溫良名士，罕豫腹心。 於是天下之人，莫不厭毒。 世隆尋讓太傅。 節閔特置儀同三師之官，位次上公之下，以世隆為之。 贈其父買珍相國、錄尚書事、大司馬。
When Shilong first served as Vice Director, he reviewed Secretariat documents at home. Quick-witted by nature and still in awe of Erzhu Rong, he applied himself rigorously to his paperwork, received guests attentively, and earned a reputation for competence. After Erzhu Rong's death, nothing held him back. As Director he routinely had Secretariat Gentlemen Song Youdao and Xing Xin hear cases at his residence, seated in separate wings east and west, taking petitions and issuing orders in his own name. With full control of the government, he held the power of life and death, indulged his appetites openly, trusted sycophants, and dispensed favor or punishment as he pleased. His brothers and cousins each commanded powerful armies, plundering the realm with unrestrained greed and cruelty. Flatterers and vicious toadies won his trust; gentle, upright men were rarely admitted to his confidence. Before long the whole realm loathed them. Shilong soon resigned the Grand Tutorship. The Jiemin Emperor created a new office, Honored Equal to the Three Preceptors, ranked just below the senior dukes, and appointed Shilong to it. He posthumously honored his father Maizhen as Chancellor of State, Recorder of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Marshal.
47
及齊神武起義兵，仲遠、度律等愚贛恃強，不以為慮，而世隆獨深憂恐。 及天光等敗于韓陵，世隆請赦天下，節閔不許。 斛斯椿既據河橋，盡殺世隆黨附，令行台長孫承業詣闕奏狀，掩執世隆及兄彥伯，俱斬之。
When Gao Huan raised his army in righteous revolt, Erzhu Zhongyuan, Erzhu Dulu, and the others—blind to the danger in their own strength—paid it no heed, but Shilong alone was deeply alarmed. After Erzhu Tianguang and the others were defeated at Hanling, Shilong pleaded for a general amnesty; the Jiemin Emperor refused. Once Husi Chun held River Bridge, he slaughtered Shilong's followers, sent Branch Commandery Chief Changsun Chengye to the palace with a report, and seized Shilong and his elder brother Erzhu Yanbo. Both were executed.
48
初，世隆曾與吏部尚書元世俊握槊，忽聞局上詨然有聲，一局子盡倒立，世隆甚惡之。 又曾晝寢，其妻奚氏忽見一人持世隆首去。 奚氏驚，就視，而世隆寢如故。 既覺，謂妻曰：「向夢人斷我頭持去，意殊不適。 」又此年正月晦日，令、僕並不上省，西門不開。 忽有河內太守田帖家奴，告省門亭長云：「今旦為令王借車牛一乘，終日于洛濱遊觀。 至晚，王還省，將車出東掖門，始覺車上無褥，請為記識。 」亭長以令僕不上，西門不開，無跡入者。 此奴固陳不已，公文列訴。 尚書都令史謝遠疑，謂妄有假借，白世隆，付曹推驗。 時都官郎中穆子容究之。 奴言，初來時，至司空府西，欲向省。 令王嫌遲，遣催車。 車入，到省西門，王嫌牛小，系于關下槐樹，更將一青牛駕車。 令王著白紗、高頂帽，短小、黑色，儐從皆裙襦袴褶，握板，不似常時服章。 遂遣一吏將奴送入省中査事東閣內，東廂第一屋中。 其屋先常閉。 奴雲，入此屋中有板床，床上無席，大有塵土，兼有甕米。 奴拂床坐，兼畫地戲，甕中米亦握看之。 子容與謝遠看之，閉極久，全無開跡。 及入，狀皆符同。 具以此對世隆。 世隆悵然，意以為惡。 未幾見誅。
On one occasion Shilong was playing pitch-pot with Minister of Personnel Yuan Shijun when a loud crack sounded on the board and every piece flipped upright at once. Shilong took it as a terrible omen. On another occasion, while he napped by day, his wife Lady Xi suddenly saw a man carrying off Shilong's head. Alarmed, she went to look—Shilong was still sleeping peacefully. When he woke he told her, "I dreamed someone cut off my head and carried it away. I feel ill at ease. On the last day of the first month that year, neither the Director nor the Vice Directors came to the Secretariat, and the western gate remained closed. Then a slave belonging to Tian Tie, Administrator of Henei commandery, reported to the Secretariat gate watch-captain: "This morning I borrowed a cart and ox for Director Wang and spent the entire day sightseeing along the Luo riverbank. In the evening Director Wang returned to the Secretariat and was about to drive out the Eastern Side Gate when he noticed the cart had no cushion and asked that this be noted. The watch-captain replied that neither the Director nor the Vice Directors had come to office, the western gate had not been opened, and no one could have entered. The slave would not drop the matter and filed a formal complaint. Secretariat Chief Clerk Xie Yuan found the story suspicious and suspected a false claim. He reported to Shilong and the case was referred for investigation. Director of Punishments Mu Zirong was assigned to investigate. The slave testified that when he first arrived he reached the area west of the Minister of Works' office and was heading for the Secretariat. Director Wang, impatient at the delay, sent someone to hurry the cart along. The cart entered and reached the Secretariat's western gate. Director Wang thought the ox too small, tied it under the catalpa tree at the gate, and swapped in a black ox. Director Wang wore white gauze and a high-topped cap. He was short and dark-complexioned. His attendants wore skirted jackets and riding trousers, clutching tablets—nothing like their usual court dress. He then sent a clerk to escort the slave into the Eastern Investigation Pavilion within the Secretariat, to the first room of the eastern wing. That room had long been kept locked. The slave said the room contained a plank bed with no mat, thick dust everywhere, and a jar of rice. The slave brushed off the bed and sat down, scratched figures on the ground for amusement, and even scooped rice from the jar to examine it. Zirong and Xie Yuan inspected the room. It had been sealed for a long time and showed no sign of entry. Yet when they opened it, every detail matched the slave's testimony. They reported the full findings to Shilong. Shilong was stricken and took it as a portent of doom. Before long he was executed.

世隆弟世承，莊帝時位侍中，領御史中尉。 人才猥劣，備員而已。 及元顥內逼，世承守轘轅，為顥所禽。 顥讓而臠之。 莊帝還宮，贈司徒。
Shilong's younger brother Shicheng served under Emperor Xiaozhuang as Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Censor-in-Chief. His abilities were crude and negligible; he was a mere figurehead. When Yuan Hao pressed inward on the capital, Shicheng held Huanyuan Pass and was captured. Yuan Hao denounced him and had him cut to pieces. When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Shicheng was posthumously honored as Minister of Education.

世承弟弼，字輔伯，節閔帝時，封河間郡公。 尋為青州刺史。 韓陵之敗，欲奔梁，數日，與左右割臂為約。 弼帳下都督馮紹隆為弼信待，乃說弼曰：「今方同契闊，宜當心瀝血，示眾以信。 」弼從之。 大集部下，弼乃踞胡床，令紹隆持刀披心。 紹隆因推刃殺之，傳首京師。
Shicheng's younger brother Bi, style name Fubo, was enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian commandery under the Jiemin Emperor. He was soon appointed Inspector of Qing province. After the defeat at Hanling, planning to flee to Liang, he and his followers cut their arms to seal a blood oath several days later. Feng Shaolong, a commander on Bi's staff whom he trusted, urged him: "We are bound in life and death together. You should open your chest and pour out your heart's blood to prove your sincerity to the men. Bi agreed. He assembled his officers. Bi seated himself on a camp chair and ordered Shaolong to take a knife and cut open his chest. Shaolong drove the blade home and killed him, then sent his head to the capital.

尒硃度律
Erzhu Dulu
52
度律，榮從父弟也，鄙樸少言。 莊帝初，封樂鄉縣伯。 榮死，與世隆赴晉陽。 元曄之立，以度律為太尉公、四面大都督，封常山王。 與尒硃兆入洛。 兆遷晉陽，留度律鎮京師。 節閔帝時，為使持節、侍中、大將軍、太尉公，兼尚書令、東北道行台，與仲遠出拒義旗。 齊神武間之，與尒硃兆遂相疑貳，自敗而還。 度律雖在軍戎，聚斂無厭，所經為百姓患毒。 其母山氏聞度律敗，遂恚憤發病。 及至，母責之曰：「汝荷國恩，無狀而反，我何忍見他屠戮汝也！ 」言終而卒，時人怪異之。 後韓陵之敗，斛斯椿先據河橋，遂西走氵壘波津，為人執送。 椿囚之，送齊神武，斬之都市。
Erzhu Dulu was Erzhu Rong's paternal cousin—crude, plain-spoken, and taciturn. At the start of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lexiang county. When Erzhu Rong was killed, Erzhu Dulu went with Erzhu Shilong to Jinyang. When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Erzhu Dulu was appointed Grand Commandant Duke and Grand Commander of the Four Fronts, and enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan. He entered Luoyang together with Erzhu Zhao. Erzhu Zhao moved to Jinyang and left Erzhu Dulu to guard the capital. Under the Jiemin Emperor he held the titles Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand General, and Grand Commandant Duke, and concurrently served as Director of the Masters of Writing and head of the Northeastern Route Mobile Secretariat, marching out with Erzhu Zhongyuan to resist Gao Huan's army of righteous revolt. Gao Huan sowed discord among them, and Erzhu Dulu and Erzhu Zhao grew mutually suspicious and disloyal, defeating themselves and retreating. Although Erzhu Dulu was on campaign, he extorted without restraint, and wherever he passed he brought misery to the common people. His mother, Lady Shan, upon hearing of Erzhu Dulu's defeat, was overcome with anger and resentment and fell ill. When he arrived, his mother rebuked him: "You owe the state a debt of gratitude, yet you rebelled without cause—how could I bear to watch others slaughter you! " With those words she died, and people of the time marveled at it. After the defeat at Hanling, Husi Chun seized the River Bridge first, and Erzhu Dulu fled west toward Loubo Ford, where he was captured and sent off under guard. Husi Chun imprisoned him and sent him to Gao Huan, who had him executed in the public marketplace.
53
尒硃天光
Erzhu Tianguang
54
天光，榮從祖兄子也。 少勇決，榮特親愛之，常預軍戎謀。 孝昌末，榮據並、肆，仍以天光為都將，總統肆州兵馬。 明帝崩，榮向京師，委以後事。 建義初，為肆州刺史，封長安縣公。 榮將討葛榮，留天光在州，鎮其根本。 謂曰：「我身不得至處，非汝無以稱我心。 」永安中，與元天穆東破邢杲。 元顥入洛，天光與天穆會榮於河內。 榮發後，並、肆不安，詔天光兼尚書僕射，為並、肆等九州行台，仍行并州事。 天光至并州，部分約勒，所在寧輯。 顥破，還京師，改封廣宗郡公。
Erzhu Tianguang was the grandson of Erzhu Rong's grand-uncle. From youth he was bold and decisive; Erzhu Rong was especially fond of him and regularly included him in military planning. In the last years of the Xiaochang reign, when Erzhu Rong held Bing and Si, he again made Erzhu Tianguang a frontier commander-in-chief and put him in overall charge of the troops and horses of Si Prefecture. When Emperor Ming died, Erzhu Rong marched toward the capital and entrusted Erzhu Tianguang with affairs at home. At the start of the Jianyi era he was appointed Inspector of Si Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Chang'an county. When Erzhu Rong set out to campaign against Ge Rong, he left Erzhu Tianguang in the province to hold his rear base secure. Erzhu Rong told him, "Where I cannot go in person, no one but you can do what I wish. " In the Yong'an era he joined Yuan Tianmu in defeating Xing Gao in the east. When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Erzhu Tianguang and Yuan Tianmu joined Erzhu Rong at Henei. After Erzhu Rong marched out, Bing and Si fell into unrest, and an edict appointed Erzhu Tianguang Concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and head of the Mobile Secretariat for Bing, Si, and seven other prefectures, while he continued to administer Bingzhou. When Erzhu Tianguang reached Bingzhou, he organized and disciplined the troops, and the region settled into calm. After Yuan Hao was defeated he returned to the capital and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Guangzong commandery.
55
初，高平鎮城人赫貴連恩等為逆，共推敕勤酋長胡琛為主，號高平王。 遙臣沃野鎮賊帥破六韓忉夤。 琛入據高平城，遣其大將万俟醜奴來寇涇州。 琛後與莫折念生交通，侮僈忉夤。 遣使人費律如至高平，誘斬琛，為醜奴所並，與蕭寶夤相拒于安定。 寶夤敗還。 建義元年夏，醜奴擊寶夤於靈州，禽之，遂僭大號。 時獲西北貢師子，因稱神獸元年，置百官。
At first He Guiyan of Gaoping garrison town and others rose in rebellion, jointly proclaiming the Chie chieftain Hu Chen their leader with the title King of Gaoping. He then offered distant allegiance to Poliuhan Huyin, the rebel leader of Woye garrison. Hu Chen entered and seized Gaoping city, then sent his great general Moqi Chounu to raid Jing Prefecture. Later Hu Chen entered into dealings with Moqi Niansheng and treated Poliuhan Huyin with contempt. Poliuhan Huyin sent an envoy, Fei Lu, to Gaoping to lure and kill Hu Chen; Moqi Chounu absorbed his forces and confronted Xiao Baoyin at Anding. Xiao Baoyin was defeated and retreated. In the summer of the first year of Jianyi, Moqi Chounu attacked Xiao Baoyin at Ling Prefecture, captured him, and then arrogated an imperial title. A tribute lion had just arrived from the northwest, and on that pretext he proclaimed the Divine Beast era and established a full court bureaucracy.
56
朝廷憂之，乃除天光使持節、都督、雍州刺史，率大都督武衛將軍賀拔岳、大都督侯莫陳悅等討醜奴。 天光初行，唯有軍士千人。 時東雍赤水蜀賊斷路，天光入關擊破之，簡取壯健。 至雍，又稅人馬，合得萬疋。 以軍人寡少，停留未進。 榮遣責之，杖天光百下。 榮復遣軍士二千人赴天光。 天光令賀拔嶽率千騎先驅，至岐州，禽其行台尉遲菩薩。 醜奴棄岐州走還安定。 天光發雍至岐，與嶽合勢，破醜奴，獲蕭寶夤。 於是涇、豳、二夏，北至靈州，及賊黨結聚之類，並降。 唯賊行台万俟道洛不下，率眾西依牽屯山，據險自守。 榮責天光不獲道洛，復遣使杖之百，詔削爵為侯。 天光與嶽、悅等復向牽屯討之，道洛戰敗，投略陽賊帥王慶雲。 慶雲以道洛驍果絕倫，得之甚喜，便謂大事可圖，乃自稱皇帝，以道洛為大將軍。 天光乃入隴，至慶雲所居永洛城，破其東城。 賊遂並趣西城。 城中無水，眾聚熱渴。 有人走降，言慶雲、道洛欲突出。 天光恐失賊帥，乃遣謂慶雲，可以早降，若水決，當聽諸人今夜共議。 又謂曰：「相知須水，今為小退。 」賊眾安悅，無復走心。 天光密使軍人多作木槍，各長七尺，至昏，布立人馬，為防衛之勢，又伏人槍中。 其夜，慶雲、道洛果突出，至槍，馬各傷倒。 伏兵便起，同時禽獲。 賊窮，乞降而已。 天光、嶽、悅等議悉阬之，死者萬七千人，分其家口。 於是三秦、河、渭、瓜、梁、鄯善咸來款順。 詔復天光前官爵。
Alarmed, the court appointed Erzhu Tianguang Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commissioner, and Inspector of Yongzhou, and ordered him to lead the Grand Commanders Martial Guard General Heba Yue, Grand Commander Houmochen Yue, and others against Moqi Chounu. When Erzhu Tianguang first set out, he had only a thousand soldiers. At the time Shu bandits at Chishui in Eastern Yong blocked the road; Erzhu Tianguang entered the passes, defeated them, and drafted the able-bodied among them. At Yong he levied men and horses as well, raising a combined force of ten thousand mounts. Because his force was still too small, he halted and did not advance. Erzhu Rong sent envoys to rebuke him and had Erzhu Tianguang beaten a hundred strokes. Erzhu Rong then sent another two thousand soldiers to reinforce Erzhu Tianguang. Erzhu Tianguang ordered Heba Yue to lead a thousand horsemen as vanguard; at Qizhou he captured the rebel Mobile Secretariat chief Yuchi Pusa. Moqi Chounu abandoned Qizhou and fled back to Anding. Erzhu Tianguang marched from Yong to Qi, joined forces with Heba Yue, defeated Moqi Chounu, and captured Xiao Baoyin. Thereupon Jing, Bin, the two Xia prefectures, and the region north to Ling Prefecture, together with every cluster of rebel bands, submitted. Only the rebel Mobile Secretariat chief Moqi Daoluo refused to submit; he led his followers west to Qiantun Mountain and held the passes in self-defense. Erzhu Rong rebuked Erzhu Tianguang for failing to capture Moqi Daoluo, again sent envoys to beat him a hundred strokes, and by edict reduced his rank to marquis. Erzhu Tianguang marched on Qiantun again with Heba Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others; Moqi Daoluo was defeated and fled to the rebel leader Wang Qingyun of Lueyang. Wang Qingyun, finding Moqi Daoluo's martial prowess unmatched, was overjoyed to have him and declared that the great enterprise could now be achieved; he styled himself emperor and made Daoluo Grand General. Erzhu Tianguang then entered Long and reached Yongluo city, where Wang Qingyun was encamped, and broke through its eastern wall. The rebels then all crowded into the western city. There was no water in the city, and the trapped masses sweltered in thirst. A deserter came over and reported that Wang Qingyun and Moqi Daoluo planned to break out. Fearing the rebel chiefs would escape, Erzhu Tianguang sent word to Wang Qingyun that he could surrender at once; if he chose to unleash the water instead, he would still allow the rebels to discuss surrender together that night. He added, "Knowing you need water, we shall pull back a little for now. " The rebel masses were reassured and no longer thought of fleeing. Erzhu Tianguang secretly ordered his soldiers to make many wooden stakes, each seven feet long; at dusk he deployed men and horses in a defensive array and hid troops among the stakes. That night Wang Qingyun and Moqi Daoluo did break out; when they reached the stakes, horse after horse was wounded and brought down. The hidden troops sprang up and captured them all at once. The rebels, driven to desperation, could only beg to surrender. Erzhu Tianguang, Heba Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others decided to massacre them all; seventeen thousand were killed, and their families were distributed as booty. Thereupon the Three Qins, the He and Wei river basins, Gua, Liang, and Shanshan all came forward to submit. An edict restored Erzhu Tianguang's former titles and enfeoffment.
57
岳聞榮死，還涇州以待，天光亦下隴，與嶽圖入洛之策。 既而莊帝進天光爵為廣宗王，元曄又以為隴西王。 及聞尒硃兆已入京，天光乃輕騎向都，見世隆等，尋便還雍。 世隆等議廢元曄，更舉親賢，遣告天光。 天光與定策，立節閔帝。 又加開府儀同三司、尚書令、關西大行台。 天光北出夏州，遣將討宿勤明達，禽之，送洛。 時費也頭帥紇豆陵伊利、万俟受洛於等據有河西，未有所附。 天光以齊神武起兵信都，內懷憂恐，不暇他事。 伊利等，但微遣備之而已。 又除大司馬。
When Heba Yue heard that Erzhu Rong was dead, he returned to Jing Prefecture to wait; Erzhu Tianguang also came down from Long and joined Heba Yue in plotting a march on Luoyang. Soon afterward Emperor Xiaozhuang advanced Erzhu Tianguang to Prince of Guangzong, and Yuan Ye in turn invested him as Prince of Longxi. When he learned that Erzhu Zhao had already entered the capital, Erzhu Tianguang rode lightly to the capital, met with Erzhu Shilong and the others, and soon returned to Yong. Erzhu Shilong and his faction deliberated deposing Yuan Ye and enthroning a close and worthy kinsman, and sent word to Erzhu Tianguang. Erzhu Tianguang joined in settling the plan and helped enthrone the Jiemin Emperor. He was further granted Opener of an Office with Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Mobile Secretariat of Guanxi. Erzhu Tianguang marched north out of Xia Prefecture, sent a general against Suqin Mingda, captured him, and sent him to Luoyang. At the time the Feiyeotou chiefs Heldouling Yili and Moqi Shouluoyu and others held Hexi and had not yet pledged themselves to any faction. Because Gao Huan had raised troops at Xindu, Erzhu Tianguang was inwardly anxious and had no leisure for other matters. As for Yili and the others, he sent only light detachments to watch them. He was further appointed Grand Marshal.
58
時神武軍既振，尒硃兆、仲遠等並經敗退。 世隆累使徵天光，天光不從。 後令斛斯椿苦要天光云：「非王無以能定，豈可坐看宗家之滅？ 」天光不得已，東下，與仲遠等敗于韓陵。 斛斯椿等先還，於河橋拒之，天光不得度，西北走，被執，與度律並送于神武。 神武送於洛，斬於都市。
By then Gao Huan's army had gained momentum, and Erzhu Zhao, Erzhu Zhongyuan, and the others had already been defeated and driven back. Erzhu Shilong repeatedly sent envoys to summon Erzhu Tianguang, but Tianguang refused to come. Later Erzhu Shilong had Husi Chun urgently press Erzhu Tianguang, saying, "Without Your Highness no one can settle matters—how can you sit by and watch the clan be destroyed? " Erzhu Tianguang had no choice; he marched east and, together with Erzhu Zhongyuan and the others, was defeated at Hanling. Husi Chun and the others returned first and blocked the River Bridge; Erzhu Tianguang could not cross, fled northwest, was captured, and was sent together with Erzhu Dulu to Gao Huan. Gao Huan sent them to Luoyang, where both were executed in the public marketplace.
59
尒硃專恣，分裂天下，各據一方，賞罰自出，而天光有定關西之功，差不酷暴，比之兆與仲遠，為不同矣。
The Erzhu clan was willful and autocratic, splitting the realm so that each branch held its own territory and dispensed rewards and punishments at will; yet Erzhu Tianguang had the achievement of pacifying Guanxi and was somewhat less cruel and violent—compared with Erzhu Zhao and Erzhu Zhongyuan, he was a different sort of man altogether.
60
論曰：魏自宣武之後，政道頗虧。 及明皇幼沖，女主南面。 始則於忠專恣，繼以元叉權重，居官者肆其聚斂，乘勢者極其陵暴，於是四海囂然，已有群飛之漸。 逮於靈後反政，宣淫於朝，傾覆之徵，於此至矣。 尒硃榮緣將帥之列，藉部眾之威，屬天下暴虐，人神怨憤。 遂有匡頹拯弊之志，援主逐惡之功。 及夫禽葛榮，誅元顥，戮邢杲，揃韓婁，醜奴、寶夤，咸梟馬市，然則榮之功烈，亦已茂矣。 而始則希覬非望，睥睨宸極，終乃靈後、少帝，沈流不反。 河陰之下，衣冠塗地，其所以得罪人神者焉。 至於末跡凶忍，地逼亦已除矣。 而朝無謀難之宰，國乏折沖之將，遂使餘孽相糾，還成嚴敵。 隆實指蹤，兆為戎首，山河失險，莊帝幽崩。 宗屬分方，作威跋扈，廢帝立主，回天倒日； 揃剝黎獻，割裂神州，刑賞任心，征伐自己。 天下之命，縣于數胡，喪亂弘多，遂至於此。 豈非天將去之，始以共定； 終於惡稔，以至殄滅。 抑亦魏紓其難，齊以驅除矣。
Commentary: From the reign of Emperor Xuanwu onward, the way of governance was greatly impaired. When Emperor Xiaoming acceded as a child, the empress dowager ruled from behind the screen. First Yu Zhong ruled with unchecked willfulness, then Yuan Cha amassed overwhelming power; officeholders plundered without restraint, and those who seized the moment bullied and oppressed to the utmost. The realm fell into uproar, and the first signs of mass upheaval were already visible. When Empress Dowager Ling resumed power, she flaunted debauchery at court, and the signs of dynastic collapse reached their fullest point. Erzhu Rong rose from the ranks of military commanders and relied on the might of his troops at a time when the realm was violently oppressed and both men and spirits seethed with resentment. He thus conceived the will to right a tottering state and rescue a ruined order, and won the achievement of supporting the ruler and driving out evil. He captured Ge Rong, executed Yuan Hao, killed Xing Gao, cut down Han Lou, and had Moqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin all displayed at the Horse Market—thus Erzhu Rong's feats of merit were indeed abundant. Yet at first he harbored illicit ambitions and looked askance at the imperial throne; in the end Empress Dowager Ling and the young emperor were drowned and never returned. At the He'yin massacre officials and gentry were strewn across the ground—that is how he earned the condemnation of both men and spirits. As for his final course, cruel and ruthless to the end, he was eliminated once his power had reached its limit. Yet the court had no minister capable of planning for crisis, and the state lacked generals to repel invaders; thus the surviving remnants entangled with one another and again became formidable enemies. Erzhu Shilong in fact directed strategy, Erzhu Zhao was the military ringleader; strategic passes and rivers were lost, and Emperor Xiaozhuang died in secret confinement. The clan kindred carved up the realm, swaggered in power, deposed emperors and enthroned new rulers, reversing heaven and overturning the sun; They stripped the common people, carved up the sacred land, dispensed punishments and rewards as their hearts pleased, and launched campaigns at their own whim. The fate of the realm hung on a handful of barbarian chieftains; calamity and disorder multiplied until the realm reached this pass. Was this not Heaven's way of removing Wei—at first using them together to stabilize the realm; and in the end, when their wickedness had fully ripened, bringing them to total extinction? Yet Wei also eased its own crisis thereby, and Qi drove the Erzhu clan out and eliminated them.
